An unreadable/absent state file reads as\n *  \"never checked\", so a first run always checks and a corrupted one self-heals. */\nfunction dueForCheck(file: string, now: number): boolean {\n  try {\n    const state = JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, \"utf8\")) as { lastCheck?: number };\n    return typeof state.lastCheck !== \"number\" || now - state.lastCheck >= CHECK_INTERVAL_MS;\n  } catch {\n    return true;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Written by installer.ts `stageRuntime`, naming the directory this runtime was copied from. */\nconst ORIGIN_FILE = \".install-origin.json\";\n\n/**\n * May this runtime be replaced automatically?\n *\n * Only when it was staged from an npx download — the documented install path, where no other tool\n * is tracking the version. `npm i -g` and a project dependency are managed by npm (an unattended\n * re-stage would leave `npm ls -g` naming a version that is no longer what runs, with no way for\n * the user to reconcile the two), and a checkout is a developer's build, which a published release\n * would silently overwrite.\n *\n * Missing marker = no. It is written on every `install`/`update` from the version that introduced\n * auto-update onward, and a machine has to re-install once to get this code at all — so a runtime\n * old enough to lack the marker is also too old to be running this check. Failing closed here\n * costs one manual install; failing open costs somebody their working tree.\n */\nexport function selfUpdatable(runtimeDir: string): boolean {\n  try {\n    const origin = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtimeDir, ORIGIN_FILE), \"utf8\")) as {\n      source?: string;\n    };\n    if (typeof origin.source !== \"string\" || !origin.source) return false;\n    // npx unpacks into a `_npx/<hash>/node_modules/...` cache directory; nothing else does.\n    return origin.source.split(/[\\\\/]/).includes(\"_npx\");\n  } catch {\n    return false; // absent or unreadable — see above, this fails closed on purpose\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Serialise updaters across concurrent sessions.\n *\n * The 24h stamp is not enough on its own: several agents starting within the same second all read\n * \"due\" before any of them has written it, so they all spawn an updater. Two `update` runs racing\n * means two `stageRuntime` calls, and staging is `rmSync(dist)` then `cpSync` — one process can\n * delete the directory the other is half way through writing, leaving a runtime with missing entry\n * points and every hook broken until a manual re-install. That burst is not hypothetical: this is\n * a plugin for machines that routinely run five agents at once.\n *\n * Same shape as deepen.ts's per-bank lock, and for the same reason — a TTL alone would wedge the\n * updater for its whole window after a crash, so the holder's pid decides liveness. The pid stored\n * is the detached CHILD's, because the copy happens in the child and outlives this process.\n *\n * In the OS temp dir, deliberately: it is scratch, and a reboot clearing it can only cost one\n * redundant check.\n */\nconst LOCK_STALE_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000;\n\nfunction lockFile(): string {\n  return join(tmpdir(), \"hindsight-coding-agent\", \"auto-update.lock\");\n}\n\nfunction acquireUpdateLock(file: string, now: number): boolean {\n  try {\n    const held = JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, \"utf8\")) as { pid?: number; ts?: number };\n    if (held.ts && now - held.ts < LOCK_STALE_MS) {\n      let holderAlive = false;\n      if (held.pid) {\n        try {\n          process.kill(held.pid, 0);\n          holderAlive = true;\n        } catch {\n          /* ESRCH: the holder died — the lock is stale NOW, not in LOCK_STALE_MS */\n        }\n      }\n      if (holderAlive) return false;\n    }\n  } catch {\n    /* no/unreadable lock — free */\n  }\n  try {\n    mkdirSync(dirname(file), { recursive: true });\n    writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify({ pid: process.pid, ts: now }));\n    return true;\n  } catch {\n    // Cannot claim the lock, so we cannot prove we are the only updater. (safe.bank as string) : resolvedId;\n  delete safe.bank;\n  return { cfg: { ...cfg, ...resolvePartial(cfg, safe as RawConfig) }, bankId };\n}\n\n/** An override section minus what it may not set: the resolution/approval fields and the nested\n *  maps (a section cannot carry sections of its own). */\nfunction overrideFields(section: object): Record<string, unknown> {\n  const safe: Record<string, unknown> = { ...section };\n  for (const k of BANK_OVERRIDE_EXCLUDED) delete safe[k];\n  delete safe.banks;\n  delete safe.paths;\n  return safe;\n}\n\n/** Resolve just the fields present in `patch`, defaulting against the CURRENT cfg (not the global\n *  defaults) so an override only changes what it names. */\nfunction resolvePartial(cfg: Config, patch: RawConfig): Partial<Config> {\n  const full = resolveConfig(patch);\n  const out: Partial<Config> = {};\n  for (const key of Object.keys(patch) as (keyof RawConfig)[]) {\n    if (key in full)\n      (out as Record<string, unknown>)[key] = (full as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)[key];\n  }\n  // The legacy key resolves into a differently-named field, so the loop above can't carry it.\n  if (\"autoReflect\" in patch && !(\"autoInject\" in patch)) out.autoInject = full.autoInject;\n  // `apiUrl` is derived from `serverMode` + `apiPort`, so an override naming any of the three\n  // re-derives all three against the current cfg: `{ serverMode: \"daemon\" }` alone must also move\n  // the URL to the local daemon, and `{ apiUrl }` under a global daemon mode stays ignored.\n  if (\"serverMode\" in patch || \"apiUrl\" in patch || \"apiPort\" in patch) {\n    const conn = resolveConfig({\n      serverMode: patch.serverMode ?? cfg.serverMode,\n      apiPort: patch.apiPort ?? cfg.apiPort,\n      apiUrl: patch.apiUrl ??       "content": "/**\n * Local daemon mode — memory with no server and no Cloud account.\n *\n * `serverMode: \"daemon\"` runs `hindsight-embed` on this machine and points the plugin at it.\n * Lifecycle is delegated to `@vectorize-io/hindsight-all`, which owns the uvx invocation, profile\n * creation, readiness polling and the macOS Metal/MPS workaround. This module only decides WHEN to\n * start it, and with what environment.\n *\n * Three connection modes, resolved in this order (the same priority the old per-agent Claude Code\n * plugin used in `scripts/lib/daemon.py`):\n *   1. an external API — Cloud or self-hosted; `serverMode` is not \"daemon\" and nothing here runs\n *   2. a healthy server already on the port — adopted as-is, never restarted, so a daemon started\n *      by an earlier session (or a server the user runs themselves) is reused\n *   3. start the daemon\n *\n * TIMING IS THE CONSTRAINT. A cold start pays for a uvx download plus model load and can take tens\n * of seconds, while the prompt hook has to return in time to not stall the user's turn. Only two\n * points therefore ensure a daemon: SessionStart, before the user has typed anything, and the Stop\n * hook, which has the longest budget and nothing waiting on its result. The prompt path does\n * nothing here at all.\n *\n * EVERY HARNESS NEEDS BOTH POINTS, not just the fresh-process hook ones. The persistent-plugin\n * hosts (opencode, Kilo, Cline, Prime Agent, dsh) run no hook binaries, so they reach these through\n * `RuntimeCore`: `seedIfCold` is their SessionStart and the write-back is their Stop. Missing that\n * is what #3524 reported — dsh in daemon mode never started a daemon, so every `hindsight_*` call\n * failed with ECONNREFUSED until the user ran `daemon-start.js` by hand. `daemon.test.ts` now fails\n * if a harness entrypoint builds a client without reaching one of the two.\n *\n * A daemon that is down is NOT special-cased anywhere downstream. Once the URL is resolved, every\n * mode uses the identical client and the identical error handling: an unreachable local daemon\n * surfaces as the same connection failure (and the same `retain_failed` diagnostic) as an\n * unreachable Cloud or self-hosted server. Skipping work because a local port was closed would have\n * made daemon mode behave differently from the other two for no benefit.\n *\n * There is no stop. One daemon serves every agent and repo on the machine, so ending one session\n * must not cut memory out from under another. Nothing retires it either: the server's idle timeout\n * was removed after it killed in-flight requests (#3903), so `daemonIdleTimeout` is inert.\n */\nimport { execFileSync, spawn as realSpawn } from \"node:child_process\";\nimport { dirname, join } from \"node:path\";\nimport { fileURLToPath } from \"node:url\";\nimport type { Config } from \"./config\";\nimport { USER_AGENT } from \"./hindsight\";\nimport { diag } from \"./diag\";\nimport { log } from \"./log\";\n\n/**\n * How long each hook is willing to block waiting for a cold daemon. Both sit well inside the\n * corresponding hook timeouts declared in harness/hook-lifecycle.ts (SessionStart 30s, Stop 60s),\n * because overrunning those gets the hook killed by the host.\n */\nexport const DAEMON_WAIT_SESSION_START_MS = 12_000;\nexport const DAEMON_WAIT_RETAIN_MS = 40_000;\n\n/** Probe a base URL's /health. Never throws — an unreachable server is just \"not running\". */\nexport async function isServerHealthy(baseUrl: string, timeoutMs = 2_000): Promise<boolean> {\n  try {\n    const res = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/health`, {\n      headers: { \"User-Agent\": USER_AGENT },\n      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs),\n    });\n    return res.ok;\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * macOS needs a CURRENT Rust toolchain to install the daemon.\n *\n * litellm — pulled in transitively by the API — publishes wheels only for manylinux and Windows\n * (verified against PyPI for 1.95.0: cp310-cp314, no macOS build for any of them). Every macOS\n * install therefore compiles it from the sdist through maturin, and its dependency tree pins a\n * recent rustc (1.94.1 at the time of writing; observed failing on 1.93.1). Only presence is\n * checked here — the required version comes from litellm's transitive crates and moves on its own\n * schedule, so pinning a number here would just go stale. A too-old toolchain still fails, but the\n * error carries the exact version needed.\n */\nexport function hasRustToolchain(): boolean {\n  if (process.platform !== \"darwin\") return true; // wheels cover linux + windows\n  try {\n    execFileSync(\"cargo\", [\"--version\"], {\n      stdio: \"pipe\",\n      timeout: 10_000,\n      windowsHide: true,\n    });\n    return true;\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Is `uv`/`uvx` on PATH? The daemon is fetched and run through it. */\nexport function hasUvx(): boolean {\n  try {\n    execFileSync(\"uvx\", [\"--version\"], {\n      stdio: \"pipe\",\n      timeout: 10_000,\n      windowsHide: true,\n    });\n    return true;\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\ninterface ProviderProbe {\n  provider: string;\n  keyEnv: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Providers the daemon can use for local fact extraction, most-specific first. Mirrors the old\n * plugin's list. `claude-code` needs no key — it drives the Claude Code CLI the user already has,\n * which is why it is the last resort rather than an error.\n */\nconst PROVIDER_PROBES: ProviderProbe[] = [\n  { provider: \"openai\", keyEnv: \"OPENAI_API_KEY\" },\n  { provider: \"anthropic\", keyEnv: \"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\" },\n  { provider: \"gemini\", keyEnv: \"GEMINI_API_KEY\" },\n  { provider: \"groq\", keyEnv: \"GROQ_API_KEY\" },\n];\n\nexport interface LlmChoice {\n  provider: string;\n  /** Absent for providers that need no credential. */\n  apiKey?: string;\n  /** Where it came from, for the installer's output and diagnostics. */\n  source: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Decide which LLM the daemon extracts facts with.\n *\n * An explicit `HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER` always wins — including for providers this code knows\n * nothing about, so a local Ollama or a gateway can be pointed at without a code change here.\n */\nexport function detectLlm(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): LlmChoice | undefined {\n  const explicit = env.HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER?.trim();\n  if (explicit) {\n    return {\n      provider: explicit,\n      apiKey: env.HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_API_KEY?.trim() || undefined,\n      source: \"HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER\",\n    };\n  }\n  for (const probe of PROVIDER_PROBES) {\n    const key = env[probe.keyEnv]?.trim();\n    if (key) return { provider: probe.provider, apiKey: key, source: probe.keyEnv };\n  }\n  if (onPath(\"claude\")) {\n    return { provider: \"claude-code\", source: \"the Claude Code CLI on PATH (no API key needed)\" };\n  }\n  return undefined;\n}\n\nfunction onPath(bin: string): boolean {\n  try {\n    execFileSync(\"which\", [bin], {\n      stdio: \"pipe\",\n      timeout: 5_000,\n      windowsHide: true,\n    });\n    return true;\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Environment handed to the daemon: the LLM choice, the idle timeout, and any HINDSIGHT_API_* the\n *  user already exports (so provider-specific knobs pass through without being enumerated here). */\nexport function daemonEnv(\n  cfg: Config,\n  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env\n): Record<string, string | undefined> {\n  const out: Record<string, string | undefined> = {};\n  // Forwarded only when set, and inert either way: the server dropped its idle timeout in #3903\n  // (it measured idleness from the request *start*, so a long retain killed its own daemon). Kept\n  // so an existing config still starts — the daemon ignores the value.\n  // It used to default to 300s here, which made the plugin the one thing on the machine opting a\n  // SHARED daemon into an auto-exit; every other integration shipped 0.\n  if (cfg.daemonIdleTimeout !== undefined) {\n    out.HINDSIGHT_EMBED_DAEMON_IDLE_TIMEOUT = String(cfg.daemonIdleTimeout);\n  }\n  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(env)) {\n    if (key.startsWith(\"HINDSIGHT_API_\") && value) out[key] = value;\n  }\n  const llm = detectLlm(env);\n  if (llm) {\n    out.HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER = llm.provider;\n    if (llm.apiKey) out.HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_API_KEY = llm.apiKey;\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\n/**\n * Launch the starter as a DETACHED process, the way seeding and the codebase survey are launched.\n *\n * A cold start pays for a uvx download plus model load and routinely outlives any hook's timeout,\n * so it cannot be awaited inline: the harness would kill the hook mid-start and the daemon would\n * never come up. The child outlives this process and keeps going.\n *\n * One spawn per cold start is the goal, and `ensureDaemon` is what holds a burst of callers to it.\n * The starter also re-checks health, so a spawn that slips through anyway leaves the daemon the\n * winner started alone — but racing starters are not free: they queue on the profile's file lock.\n */\nexport function startDaemonDetached(\n  cfg: Config,\n  harness: string,\n  spawnFn: typeof realSpawn = realSpawn\n): void {\n  try {\n    const starter = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), \"daemon-start.js\");\n    const child = spawnFn(\"node\", [starter, \"--harness\", harness], {\n      detached: true,\n      stdio: \"ignore\",\n      windowsHide: true,\n    });\n    // spawn() failures often surface ASYNCHRONOUSLY as an 'error' event; unhandled, that would\n    // crash the hook.\n    child.on(\"error\", () => {});\n    child.unref();\n    diag(harness, \"daemon_start_spawned\", { apiUrl: cfg.apiUrl });\n  } catch {\n    /* best-effort: a failed spawn must not break the caller */\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Cold starts currently in flight, keyed by API URL.\n *\n * Every ensure point re-checks health and starts its own daemon when the port is dead, and the\n * persistent-plugin hosts fire several of them within the same tick — one SessionStart per session\n * plus a Stop per finished turn. Each of them therefore observes the same dead port before the\n * first daemon answers, and each spawns a starter of its own. The starters then serialise on the\n * profile's file lock, where the losers sit for the full 300 s lock budget before failing\n * (#1155, #3100). One entry per URL collapses that burst onto a single spawn.\n *\n * Keyed by URL rather than held as a module singleton because a caller may be pointed at any\n * daemon port. The entry is dropped as soon as its attempt settles, so a later turn that still\n * finds the port dead starts a fresh attempt instead of inheriting a spent one.\n *\n * Module-global, and deliberately without a lock: Node runs one thread, and the check-then-set\n * below contains no `await`, so two callers cannot interleave between the `get` and the `set`.\n */\nconst coldStarts = new Map<string, Promise<void>>();\n\n/**\n * Await `p` for at most `ms`. The timer is cleared on the way out: a follower that gives up early\n * must not leave an abandoned `setTimeout` holding the hook process open behind it.\n */\nasync function waitBounded(p: Promise<void>, ms: number): Promise<void> {\n  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;\n  try {\n    await Promise.race([\n      p,\n      new Promise<void>((resolve) => {\n        timer = setTimeout(resolve, Math.max(ms, 0));\n      }),\n    ]);\n  } finally {\n    clearTimeout(timer);\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Make sure a daemon is serving `cfg.apiUrl`. A no-op in every other mode.\n *\n * Side effect only — callers proceed regardless of whether it came up, so that a request against a\n * down daemon fails through exactly the same path as a request against a down Cloud or self-hosted\n * server. Never throws: memory is best-effort and must not break the agent.\n *\n * `waitMs` bounds how long the caller is willing to block for a cold start — always well under the\n * calling hook's own timeout, so a slow start costs memory for one turn rather than a killed hook.\n *\n * A start already underway is joined rather than duplicated; see `coldStarts`.\n */\nexport async function ensureDaemon(\n  cfg: Config,\n  harness: string,\n  opts: { waitMs?: number; spawnFn?: typeof realSpawn } = {}\n): Promise<void> {\n  if (cfg.serverMode !== \"daemon\") return;\n  if (await isServerHealthy(cfg.apiUrl)) return;\n  if (!preflightDaemon(cfg, harness)) return;\n\n  const waitMs = opts.waitMs ?? 0;\n  const running = coldStarts.get(cfg.apiUrl);\n  if (running) {\n    // Join the start already underway instead of spawning a competitor, so a burst costs one\n    // starter rather than one per caller. Never for longer than this caller's own budget — a Stop\n    // hook waiting 40 s must not push a SessionStart hook past its 30 s timeout — and whatever is\n    // left of that budget once the shared attempt settles goes on waiting for the daemon the\n    // attempt set in motion, so joining never leaves a caller with less patience than it would\n    // have had on its own.\n    const startedAt = Date.now();\n    // Awaited for its side effect only: a follower does not inherit the attempt's failure.\n    await waitBounded(\n      running.catch(() => undefined),\n      waitMs\n    );\n    const remaining = waitMs - (Date.now() - startedAt);\n    if (remaining > 0) await waitForHealth(cfg.apiUrl, remaining);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const attempt = (async () => {\n    startDaemonDetached(cfg, harness, opts.spawnFn);\n    await waitForHealth(cfg.apiUrl, waitMs);\n  })();\n  coldStarts.set(cfg.apiUrl, attempt);\n  try {\n    await attempt;\n  } finally {\n    // Only the owner clears the entry, so a follower can never drop a newer attempt's guard.\n    if (coldStarts.get(cfg.apiUrl) === attempt) coldStarts.delete(cfg.apiUrl);\n  }\n}\n\n/** Poll /health until it answers or the budget runs out. `budgetMs <= 0` means \"don't wait\". */\nexport async function waitForHealth(\n  baseUrl: string,\n  budgetMs: number,\n  pollMs = 1_000\n): Promise<boolean> {\n  const deadline = Date.now() + budgetMs;\n  while (Date.now() < deadline) {\n    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, pollMs));\n    if (await isServerHealthy(baseUrl)) return true;\n  }\n  return false;\n}\n\n/** The two things daemon mode cannot work without. Reported, never thrown. */\nexport function preflightDaemon(cfg: Config, harness: string): boolean {\n  if (!hasUvx()) {\n    diag(harness, \"daemon_uvx_missing\", { apiUrl: cfg.apiUrl });\n    log.warn(harness, \"daemon mode needs `uv` on PATH — see https://docs.astral.sh/uv/\");\n    return false;\n  }\n  if (!hasRustToolchain()) {\n    diag(harness, \"daemon_rust_missing\", { platform: process.platform });\n    log.warn(\n      harness,\n      \"daemon mode on macOS needs a current Rust toolchain (litellm ships no macOS wheel) — \" +\n        \"install from https://rustup.rs, then `rustup default stable && rustup update`\"\n    );\n    return false;\n  }\n  if (!detectLlm()) {\n    diag(harness, \"daemon_no_llm\", {});\n    log.warn(\n      harness,\n      \"daemon mode needs an LLM for fact extraction — set OPENAI_API_KEY (or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / \" +\n        \"GEMINI_API_KEY / HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER), or install the Claude Code CLI\"\n    );\n    return false;\n  }\n  return true;\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * Harness-agnostic Hindsight HTTP client (raw fetch, no SDK dep).\n *\n * Every harness adapter and the backfill CLI go through this one client: it configures the bank\n * (missions + git/chat retain strategies), retains memories, reflects, drains async operations, and\n * creates knowledge pages. Nothing here knows about opencode/claude-code/etc.\n */\nimport {\n  type BankOverrides,\n  buildPageTrigger,\n  codingBankManifest,\n  type CustomPagesConfig,\n  type CurrentPageTrigger,\n  PAGE_MAX_TOKENS,\n  pagesFor,\n  type PagesConfig,\n  pageScopeRule,\n  type PageTrigger,\n  pageTriggerDrifted,\n  pageTriggerFor,\n  pageTriggerPatch,\n  type RetainExtractionMode,\n} from \"./missions\";\nimport { version as PKG_VERSION } from \"../../package.json\";\nimport { pool, semverGte, sleep } from \"./util\";\nimport type { RetainStamp } from \"./retain-stamp\";\n\n/** Sent on every request so the server can tell which integration is calling. */\nexport const USER_AGENT = `hindsight-coding-agents/${PKG_VERSION}`;\n\n/** One node of GET /knowledge-base/tree. Only the fields this client reads. */\nexport interface KnowledgeNode {\n  id: string;\n  kind: \"folder\" | \"page\";\n  name: string;\n  /** The page's source query (OKF `description`) — what a re-sync compares against. */\n  description?: string;\n  /** The page's EFFECTIVE refresh policy, on servers new enough to report it (#3572). Absent\n   *  everywhere else, which `seedPages()` reads as \"unknown, leave it alone\". */\n  trigger?: CurrentPageTrigger;\n  children?: KnowledgeNode[];\n}\n\n/**\n * How consolidation scopes the observations a retained memory feeds (`observation_scopes` on the\n * retain API). The scalar modes are the server's; a `string[][]` declares the scopes explicitly.\n */\nexport type ObservationScopes =\n  | \"shared\"\n  | \"combined\"\n  | \"per_tag\"\n  | \"all_combinations\"\n  | \"per_source\"\n  | string[][];\n\n/**\n * `per_source` is resolved HERE, per document, and never reaches the server: it expands to the\n * global scope plus one named for that document's own `source:` tag.\n *\n * It cannot be expressed as configuration. The server treats an explicit scope list as\n * unconditional — consolidation returns it verbatim without filtering it against the memory's own\n * tags — so a configured `[[], [\"source:git\"], [\"source:chat\"]]` writes EVERY document into all\n * three, and the `source:git` scope fills up with beliefs built from chat transcripts. Only a\n * per-document decision separates \"what the commits say\" from \"what was discussed\".\n *\n * `per_tag` would split on the right axis but also on every other one: it reinstates the per-agent\n * `harness:` fork that `shared` exists to prevent, and any volatile tag (a session id in\n * `retainTags`) becomes its own scope, which is the fragmentation bug itself. Reading only\n * `source:` is what keeps this safe.\n *\n * A document may carry more than one source tag — the commit-message seed is both `source:git` and\n * `source:git-log`, because the cold-repo check filters on `source:git` — so every distinct one\n * gets a scope. Taking all of them, sorted, is the only rule that needs no arbitrary tie-break and\n * does not silently depend on the order the caller assembled its tags in.\n *\n * The empty scope is always first and always present, so the untagged observations that knowledge\n * pages read (they match with `tags_match: \"all\"`) keep being written exactly as under `shared`.\n */\nexport function resolveRetainScopes(\n  tags: string[] | undefined,\n  configured: ObservationScopes\n): ObservationScopes {\n  if (configured !== \"per_source\") return configured;\n  const sources = [...new Set((tags ?? []).filter((t) => t.startsWith(\"source:\")))].sort();\n  return [[], ...sources.map((s) => [s])];\n}\n\n/**\n * One global scope for everything this plugin writes.\n *\n * The server default (`combined`) scopes an observation to the memory's WHOLE tag set, and every\n * document we write carries provenance tags — `source:chat`, `harness:<id>`, `knowledge:<kind>`,\n * anything from `retainTags`. That splits one repository's knowledge into a separate observation\n * set per tag combination: work the same repo with two agents and the harness tag alone gives two\n * parallel sets of beliefs that never merge, each blind to the other, at double the consolidation\n * cost (#3564). Those tags are provenance — they say who wrote a memory, not which project the\n * belief is about — so they belong on the facts (where they still filter recall) and not on the\n * consolidation boundary. `shared` keeps them on the facts and consolidates into ONE untagged\n * scope per bank, which is what a bank already is: one project's memory.\n */\nexport const DEFAULT_OBSERVATION_SCOPES: ObservationScopes = \"shared\";\n\nexport interface ClientOpts {\n  apiUrl: string;\n  apiToken?: string;\n  bank: string;\n  /** Repository this bank is about, named in every page query this client writes\n   *  (`pageScopeRule`). Undefined when no single repository is (a shared static bank, a path map, a\n   *  bank several repos are renamed onto) — the query then gets the shared-bank clause, which\n   *  names no project (#4490). Must be a property of the bank and never of the calling session's\n   *  cwd: see `bankProjectName` (#4146). */\n  project?: string;\n  log?: (msg: string) => void;\n  /** Cap on concurrent retain-related requests (drain op polls, deepen pools). Default 10. */\n  maxParallelRetains?: number;\n  /** Observation scoping for every retain this client sends. Default `DEFAULT_OBSERVATION_SCOPES`. */\n  observationScopes?: ObservationScopes;\n  /** Pages one knowledge-page search returns. Default `DEFAULT_PAGE_SEARCH_LIMIT`. Lives on the\n   *  client so every caller — the hook's injection and the MCP tool — shares one value. */\n  pageSearchLimit?: number;\n  /** Recall-body overrides, merged key-by-key over `DEFAULT_RECALL_OPTIONS`. Passed through to\n   *  the API as given (`types`, `max_tokens`, `budget`, …); `query` is never overridable. */\n  recallOptions?: Record<string, unknown>;\n  /** Re-read the bearer token from the LIVE config, for hosts that outlive their credential.\n   *  `apiToken` alone is a construction-time snapshot: a long-lived host (dsh, Cline, Kilo, the\n   *  MCP server, any persistent plugin) kept signing with it forever, so enabling auth or rotating\n   *  the key mid-session 401'd every call until the host restarted (#3600). Consulted only on a\n   *  401, so the happy path never touches the filesystem. Journaling under `retainSessions: false` writes a temp file nothing reads,\n  // which is cheaper than threading that decision through two processes to find out.\n  if (spec.journalPrompt) {\n    appendJournalTurn(journalPath(spec.harness, sessionId), { role: \"user\", content: prompt });\n  }\n\n  const out = (context: string | undefined, notice?: string) =>\n    process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(spec.emit(context ?? \"\", notice, ev)));\n\n  const sessionRoot = sessionRootDir(spec.harness, sessionId, cwd);\n  const derived = deriveBankIdOrSkip(cfg, cwd, spec.harness, sessionRoot);\n  if (derived === null) return; // repository unidentifiable: stay silent rather than invent a bank\n  const resolved = applyBankConfig(cfg, derived, cwd);\n  cfg = resolved.cfg;\n  const bankId = resolved.bankId;\n  if (cfg.disabled) {\n    log.debug(spec.harness, \"hook skipped: bank disabled via banks override\", { bank: bankId });\n    return;\n  }\n  const client = makeClient({\n    apiUrl: cfg.apiUrl,\n    apiToken: cfg.apiToken,\n    bank: bankId,\n    maxParallelRetains: cfg.maxParallelRetains,\n    observationScopes: cfg.observationScopes,\n    pageSearchLimit: cfg.pageSearchLimit,\n    recallOptions: cfg.recallOptions,\n  });\n  const cacheFile = sessionCacheFile(spec.harness, sessionId || \"no-session\");\n\n  // Safety net on EVERY harness: on the session's FIRST prompt (no cache file yet), fire the\n  // ingestion engine. Normally the shared SessionStart lifecycle already did — the engine's\n  // per-bank lock makes this a no-op — but a session that predates installation never received\n  // SessionStart. This limited fallback heals that case without duplicating any survey logic.\n  if (cfg.autoSeed !== false && !existsSync(cacheFile)) {\n    startBackgroundSeed(cwd, { limit: cfg.seedLimit, harness: spec.harness });\n  }\n\n  const output = await buildHookOutput({ harness: spec.harness, prompt, cfg, client, cacheFile });\n  // Mid-session heal: a bank with ZERO pages means the engine never built it (e.g. the session\n  // predates the install, so no SessionStart and the first-prompt net already passed). Fire the\n  // idempotent engine — the per-bank lock makes repeats free while it builds.\n  if (\n    cfg.autoSeed !== false &&\n    client.knowledgePagesSupported !== false &&\n    output.pages.length === 0\n  ) {\n    startBackgroundSeed(cwd, { limit: cfg.seedLimit, harness: spec.harness });\n  }\n  let context = output.context;\n  if (context && spec.toolHook && sessionId) {\n    stashPendingContext(spec.harness, sessionId, context);\n    context = undefined;\n  }\n  if (context || output.notice) out(context, output.notice);\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "hindsight-integrations/coding-agents/src/core/host-client.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * ONE place a long-lived host turns \"which repo am I serving\" into a configured client.\n *\n * Every persistent host (dsh, Cline, Kilo, Prime Agent, opencode and the other plugin entries, the\n * MCP server) used to carry its own copy of the same four steps — loadConfig, deriveBankId,\n * applyBankConfig, `new HindsightClient({...})`. Five copies of a block is five chances to leave a\n * field out, and two already had: dsh and Prime Agent never passed `maxParallelRetains` (so both\n * silently ignored that setting), and dsh never passed the directory to `applyBankConfig` (so\n * `optInOnly` was not enforced there at all). #3600 was the same shape a third time — the\n * credential snapshot — which is why the fix is one shared builder rather than a sixth line added\n * to each host.\n *\n * The one-shot CLIs (`status.ts`, `deepen.ts`) stay out: they resolve config from `--config`/\n * `--harness` flags rather than from a workspace, and their process ends long before a credential\n * can rotate under them.\n */\nimport { applyBankConfig, loadConfig, type Config } from \"./config\";\nimport { bankProjectName, deriveBankIdOrSkip } from \"./bank\";\nimport { HindsightClient } from \"./hindsight\";\n\n/** A host's resolved memory: the config for THIS workspace, the bank it resolved to, and a client\n *  bound to both. */\nexport interface HostMemory {\n  cfg: Config;\n  bankId: string;\n  client: HindsightClient;\n}\n\n/** Resolve config for one workspace: env + file + `harnesses.<name>`, then the `banks.<id>`\n *  section for the bank that directory maps to, with `optInOnly` enforced. */\nexport function resolveHostConfig(\n  harness: string,\n  directory: string\n): { cfg: Config; bankId: string; project?: string } {\n  const cfg0 = loadConfig({ harness });\n  // A globally disabled plugin stops HERE, before bank derivation: `disabled` exists to be a\n  // zero-overhead baseline — the same agent with no memory — not merely a silent one. Callers\n  // return early on `cfg.disabled`, so the empty bank id never reaches a request.\n  if (cfg0.disabled) return { cfg: cfg0, bankId: \"\" };\n  const bankId = deriveBankIdOrSkip(cfg0, directory, harness);\n  // An unidentifiable repository takes the same exit: no bank id is safer than a guessed one, and\n  // `disabled` is the signal every caller already handles (#3950).\n  if (bankId === null) return { cfg: { ...cfg0, disabled: true }, bankId: \"\" };\n  const resolved = applyBankConfig(cfg0, bankId, directory);\n  // The repository the bank is ABOUT, for page scoping — the same rule as deepen.ts: only a bank\n  // that is this repo's, not one a `banks.<id>.bank` rename points several repos at (#4490).\n  const project = resolved.bankId === bankId ? bankProjectName(resolved.cfg, directory) : undefined;\n  return { ...resolved, project };\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve config for `directory` and build the client for it.\n *\n * Callers still decide what a disabled config means for them (skip registration, cache a null\n * workspace, expose no tools) — `cfg.disabled` on the returned config already accounts for both\n * the global switch and the per-bank opt-out. Building a client has no side effect: nothing is\n * sent until a caller asks for something.\n */\nexport function resolveHostMemory(harness: string, directory: string): HostMemory {\n  const { cfg, bankId, project } = resolveHostConfig(harness, directory);\n  return {\n    cfg,\n    bankId,\n    client: new HindsightClient({\n      apiUrl: cfg.apiUrl,\n      apiToken: cfg.apiToken,\n      bank: bankId,\n      // Names the repo in the initiative pages this host captures, as the seeded pages do.\n      project,\n      maxParallelRetains: cfg.maxParallelRetains,\n      observationScopes: cfg.observationScopes,\n      pageSearchLimit: cfg.pageSearchLimit,\n      recallOptions: cfg.recallOptions,\n      // The credential a host STARTED with is not the one it must keep using: enable auth or\n      // rotate the key mid-session and the snapshot 401s every call until restart (#3600). Read\n      // through the same pipeline the constructor used, so a per-bank `banks.<id>.apiToken` is\n      // honoured on re-resolution exactly as it was on the first one.\n      // The URL stays the one this client was built with, so a token re-read after the config\n      // moved this directory to ANOTHER server is that server's credential: never send it here.\n      tokenProvider: () => {\n        const live = resolveHostConfig(harness, directory).cfg;\n        return live.apiUrl === cfg.apiUrl ? live.apiToken : cfg.apiToken;\n      },\n    }),\n  };\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "hindsight-integrations/coding-agents/src/core/knowledge-tools.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Knowledge-page MCP tool specs — runtime SDK-free so this stays unit-testable without a real MCP\n * host.\n *\n * `src/mcp-server.ts` is the only file with a runtime MCP SDK import; this module uses only its\n * `ToolAnnotations` type. The server wires the specs returned here into an `McpServer`. Each tool\n * wraps one `HindsightClient` knowledge-page/recall method: it never throws — a thrown client error\n * is caught and turned into an `isError:true` text result so the calling LLM sees the failure\n * instead of the process crashing.\n *\n * The agent-facing surface is intentionally curated: grounding + capture only. Raw page CRUD\n * (create/update/delete) is deliberately NOT exposed — agents never author page structure; they\n * capture initiatives (`hindsight_capture_initiative`) and pages are synthesized/maintained by the\n * server. `hindsight_ingest_document` (raw-content retain) also backs the codebase survey\n * (core/survey.ts).\n */\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\nimport { createHash } from \"node:crypto\";\nimport { existsSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport { homedir } from \"node:os\";\nimport { join } from \"node:path\";\nimport type { ToolAnnotations } from \"@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js\";\nimport type { ZodRawShape } from \"zod\";\nimport type { HindsightClient } from \"./hindsight\";\nimport { syncStatus } from \"./status\";\nimport { applyBankConfig, DEFAULT_REFLECT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS, loadConfig } from \"./config\";\nimport { diagFilePath } from \"./diag\";\nimport { describeError } from \"./log\";\nimport type { RetainStamp } from \"./retain-stamp\";\nimport type { PageTrigger } from \"./missions\";\n\nexport interface ToolResult {\n  // Index signature so this structurally satisfies the MCP SDK's CallToolResult (which carries\n  // extra optional fields we don't set) when passed to `McpServer.tool()` in src/mcp-server.ts —\n  // the only file that imports the SDK; this file stays SDK-free.\n  [x: string]: unknown;\n  content: { type: \"text\"; text: string }[];\n  isError?: boolean;\n}\n\ntype ToolSafetyAnnotations = Required<\n  Pick<ToolAnnotations, \"readOnlyHint\" | \"destructiveHint\" | \"idempotentHint\" | \"openWorldHint\">\n>;\n\nconst READ_ONLY_ANNOTATIONS: ToolSafetyAnnotations = {\n  readOnlyHint: true,\n  destructiveHint: false,\n  idempotentHint: true,\n  openWorldHint: false,\n};\n\nconst NON_DESTRUCTIVE_WRITE_ANNOTATIONS: ToolSafetyAnnotations = {\n  readOnlyHint: false,\n  destructiveHint: false,\n  idempotentHint: false,\n  openWorldHint: false,\n};\n\n/**\n * Returned alongside every search result set.\n *\n * Phrased as an obligation triggered by the CALL, not by the agent judging that it \"used\" a page: a\n * model that paraphrases a snippet into its own prose does not register itself as having quoted\n * anything, and silently absorbs the memory instead of crediting it.\n */\nconst CREDIT_REMINDER =\n  \"Crediting is mandatory, not a judgement call: if anything these results contribute reaches your \" +\n  \"reply — quoted, paraphrased, or merely confirming what you were going to say — open that part \" +\n  'with \"> 🧠 **From Hindsight memory (<page>)** — <the specific facts you drew on>\". Rewriting a ' +\n  \"snippet in your own words does not make it yours. If none of them bear on the turn, ignore them \" +\n  \"silently — an unhelpful search needs no mention. These are past records: check a claim that \" +\n  \"something was fixed or works against the code before relying on it.\";\n\nexport interface ToolSpec {\n  name: string;\n  description: string;\n  inputSchema: ZodRawShape;\n  /**\n   * Safety metadata published verbatim as the tool's MCP annotations (src/mcp-server.ts).\n   *\n   * Required, not optional: it is not cosmetic. Dcode gates every MCP tool lacking a coherent\n   * read-only annotation behind an approval prompt, so in its headless (`dcode -n`) runtime an\n   * unannotated tool is REJECTED outright — \"This MCP action requires approval, but the current\n   * headless runtime has no approval UI.\" Codex Auto-review likewise treats an unannotated call as\n   * unverified external access. Reads get READ_ONLY_ANNOTATIONS; the two writes get\n   * NON_DESTRUCTIVE_WRITE_ANNOTATIONS so clients still gate them, but for the right reason.\n   */\n  annotations: ToolSafetyAnnotations;\n  handler: (args: any) => Promise<ToolResult>;\n}\n\nfunction ok(value: unknown): ToolResult {\n  return { content: [{ type: \"text\", text: JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) }] };\n}\n\nfunction err(e: unknown): ToolResult {\n  const message = describeError(e);\n  return { content: [{ type: \"text\", text: JSON.stringify({ error: message }) }], isError: true };\n}\n\n/** Wrap a handler body so a thrown client error always becomes an isError:true result, never a throw. */\nfunction guarded(fn: (args: any) => Promise<unknown>): (args: any) => Promise<ToolResult> {\n  return async (args: any) => {\n    try {\n      return ok(await fn(args));\n    } catch (e) {\n      return err(e);\n    }\n  };\n}\n\n/** Build the knowledge-page + recall MCP tool specs, bound to one client/bank. */\nexport function buildKnowledgeTools(\n  client: HindsightClient,\n  bankId: string,\n  opts: {\n    repoDir?: string;\n    harness?: string;\n    stampFor?: () => RetainStamp;\n    /** Refresh policy for a page `hindsight_capture_initiative` creates (core/missions.ts). */\n    pageTrigger?: PageTrigger;\n    /** How long `hindsight_reflect` waits on the server (cfg.reflectToolTimeoutMs). Must be\n     *  threaded in by every caller: left unset, the client falls back to a 120s deadline that\n     *  aborts high-budget synthesis on a populated bank mid-flight (#3590). */\n    reflectTimeoutMs?: number;\n    /** Reflect budget for `hindsight_reflect` (cfg.reflectBudget, default \"high\"). */\n    reflectBudget?: \"low\" | \"mid\" | \"high\";\n    /** cfg.toolGuideExtra, added after the crediting note so it lands with the results too. */\n    toolGuideExtra?: string;\n  } = {}\n): ToolSpec[] {\n  const extra = opts.toolGuideExtra?.trim();\n  const crediting = extra ? `${CREDIT_REMINDER} ${extra}` : CREDIT_REMINDER;\n  return [\n    {\n      name: \"hindsight_sync_status\",\n      description:\n        \"Report whether this repo's memory bank is in sync: gitlog seed present, how much recent \" +\n        \"history has been deepened with full diffs, conversations ingested, knowledge pages \" +\n        \"created, and extractions still running. `synced: true` means the seeded memory is fully \" +\n        \"queryable. Ingestion is automatic and background — if not synced, it is in progress; \" +\n        \"nothing to run.\",\n      inputSchema: {},\n      annotations: READ_ONLY_ANNOTATIONS,\n      handler: async () => {\n        try {\n          return ok(await syncStatus(client, bankId, opts.repoDir ?? process.cwd()));\n        } catch (e) {\n          return err(e);\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: \"hindsight_diagnose\",\n      description:\n        \"Report safe Hindsight runtime diagnostics for this coding-agent session: resolved bank, \" +\n        \"workspace, harness, config location, API endpoint, and non-secret environment overrides. \" +\n        \"Use this when memory, hooks, MCP tools, or configuration appear not to work. Tokens and \" +\n        \"other secret values are never returned.\",\n      inputSchema: {},\n      annotations: READ_ONLY_ANNOTATIONS,\n      handler: async (_args: Record<string, never>) => {\n        const configPath =\n          process.env.HINDSIGHT_CONFIG || join(homedir(), \".hindsight\", \"coding-agent.json\");\n        const harness = opts.harness ?? \"unknown\";\n        // Resolve through the SAME pipeline the host used — including the `banks.<id>` section for\n        // the bank this client is bound to, which may carry its own apiToken/apiUrl. A bare\n        // loadConfig() would report a mismatch for every per-bank credential.\n        const cfg = applyBankConfig(\n          loadConfig({ harness: opts.harness }),\n          bankId,\n          opts.repoDir\n        ).cfg;\n        return ok({\n          bank_id: bankId,\n          harness,\n          workspace: opts.repoDir ?? process.cwd(),\n          config: {\n            path: configPath,\n            exists: existsSync(configPath),\n            api_url: cfg.apiUrl,\n            api_token_configured: Boolean(cfg.apiToken),\n            disabled: cfg.disabled,\n          },\n          // What the LIVE client is signing with, which is not the same question as what the file\n          // says. A long-lived host used to keep a credential the config had already replaced, and\n          // this tool reported that state as perfectly healthy (#3600). Booleans only — the token\n          // value is never returned.\n          credential: {\n            api_token_in_use: Boolean(client.apiToken),\n            api_token_matches_config: client.apiToken === cfg.apiToken,\n          },\n          environment: {\n            config_override: Boolean(process.env.HINDSIGHT_CONFIG),\n            hooks_disabled: Boolean(process.env.HINDSIGHT_DISABLE_HOOKS),\n            log_level: process.env.HINDSIGHT_LOG_LEVEL ?? null,\n            diagnostics_file: diagFilePath(),\n            channel_id_configured: Boolean(process.env.HINDSIGHT_CHANNEL_ID),\n            user_id_configured: Boolean(process.env.HINDSIGHT_USER_ID),\n          },\n        });\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: \"hindsight_search_knowledge_pages\",\n      description:\n        \"Search this repository's Hindsight knowledge pages for content relevant to a query — \" +\n        \"hybrid full-text + semantic search, server-side. Call this when the user's question may \" +\n        \"be answered by the project's accumulated knowledge (architecture, conventions, decisions, \" +\n        \"initiatives) rather than by reading code. Returns ranked pages with a relevance snippet; \" +\n        // Same sentence the payload carries, from the same constant: two copies of a rule this\n        // fiddly drift apart, and the description is what a host shows when the tool is listed.\n        \"read a full page with hindsight_read_knowledge_page. \" +\n        crediting,\n      inputSchema: { query: z.string().describe(\"what to look for\") },\n      annotations: READ_ONLY_ANNOTATIONS,\n      handler: async (args: { query: string }) => {\n        try {\n          // Limit comes from the client (`pageSearchLimit`), so the tool and the hook's injection\n          // can never drift apart — this used to pass its own literal 3.\n          const hits = await client.searchKnowledgePages(args.query);\n          // No `score`. The server fuses BM25 and vector search with reciprocal rank fusion, so the\n          // number is ~1/(60+rank) summed over two retrievers: a perfect top hit scores about 0.03\n          // and nothing ever approaches 1. Handed that, a model reads a strong match as 3% relevant\n          // and discounts it. The hits arrive in rank order, which is the ranking that means\n          // something here.\n          // The reminder rides WITH the hits, not only in the session guide. Measured on real\n          // sessions: the agent searched, got ten on-topic pages, wrote an answer built from them\n          // and credited nothing — then credited correctly the moment the user asked \"where did you\n          // see that?\". The guide had scrolled far up the context by then; the instruction that\n          // lands at the same moment as the results is the one that can still be acted on.\n          return ok({\n            pages: hits.map((h) => ({\n              page: h.name,\n              page_id: h.id,\n              // The question the page answers — the same `description` the list and read tools\n              // carry, so a hit says what the page is FOR, not just how it opens.\n              ...(h.source_query ? { description: h.source_query } : {}),\n              snippet: h.snippet,\n            })),\n            crediting,\n          });\n        } catch (e) {\n          return err(e);\n        }\n      },\n    },\n    {\n      name: \"hindsight_list_knowledge_pages\",\n      description:\n        \"List this repository's Hindsight knowledge pages — curated, continuously-updated \" +\n        \"summaries of the project's durable knowledge (architecture, components, conventions, key \" +\n        \"decisions, and in-flight initiatives). Returns each page's id, title, and a one-line \" +\n        \"description of what it covers. Call this at the start of any non-trivial task, and again \" +\n        \"periodically in long sessions, to see what the project already knows before you read code \" +\n        \"or ask the user. The list changes as work is captured, so re-check it occasionally.\",\n      inputSchema: {},\n      annotations: READ_ONLY_ANNOTATIONS,\n      handler: guarded(async () => client.listPages()),\n    },\n    {\n      name: \"hindsight_read_knowledge_page\",\n      description:\n        \"Read the full content of one knowledge page by its id (from \" +\n        \"hindsight_list_knowledge_pages). Call this whenever a listed page is relevant to what \" +\n        \"you're about to do — e.g. read Conventions before writing new code, Component map before \" +\n        \"changing a subsystem, or an initiative's page before continuing that feature. A page may \" +\n        \"contain [[page:<id>]] links to related pages; follow one by calling this tool again with \" +\n        \"that id. Prefer reading a page over re-deriving the same understanding from source.\",\n      inputSchema: { page_id: z.string() },\n      annotations: READ_ONLY_ANNOTATIONS,\n      handler: guarded(async ({ page_id }) => client.getPage(page_id)),\n    },\n    {\n      name: \"hindsight_reflect\",\n      description:\n        \"Deep memory reasoning: an agentic synthesis over this repository's FULL memory (git \" +\n        \"decisions, past sessions, ingested knowledge) that answers WHY questions — the past \" +\n        \"decision and exact rule/values that explain a behavior, bug, or convention. Slower than \" +\n        \"hindsight_search_knowledge_pages (several seconds): reach for it when pages are too \" +\n        \"shallow and you need the root cause or the decided literals. When the answer informs \" +\n        'your reply, credit it visibly with a blockquote header: \"> 🧠 **From Hindsight memory** — <summary>\".',\n      inputSchema: { query: z.string().describe(\"the question to reason over memory about\") },\n      annotations: READ_ONLY_ANNOTATIONS,\n      handler: guarded(async ({ query }: { query: string }) =>\n        client.reflect(query, {\n          budget: opts.reflectBudget ?? \"high\",\n          timeoutMs: opts.reflectTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_REFLECT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS,\n        })\n      ),\n    },\n    {\n      name: \"hindsight_capture_initiative\",\n      description:\n        \"Record a new feature or initiative as a tracked knowledge page, so future sessions know it \" +\n        \"exists and can build on it — and keep that page tracking the plan as it moves.\\n\\n\" +\n        \"WHEN TO CALL:\\n\" +\n        \"- Starting one: right after the user approves a plan or finishes brainstorming a new feature/\" +\n        \"capability and you are about to start implementing — BEFORE you write any code. Leave \" +\n        \"relates_to_page_id empty.\\n\" +\n        \"- Plan changed: call it AGAIN — mid-implementation is fine and expected — whenever the goal, \" +\n        \"scope, or rationale of an initiative you already captured materially changes (an approach is \" +\n        \"dropped, scope grows or shrinks, the why is rewritten). Pass relates_to_page_id = that \" +\n        \"initiative's page id so the change lands on the existing page. Never mint a second page for the \" +\n        \"same initiative.\\n\\n\" +\n        \"WHEN TO SKIP: bug fixes, small tweaks, refactors, chores, and trivial course-corrections that \" +\n        \"leave the goal intact are not initiatives — skip them.\\n\\n\" +\n        \"- title: short, specific name (e.g. 'Newsletter refinement chat'). On a recapture, reuse the \" +\n        \"initiative's existing title.\\n\" +\n        \"- summary: 2-3 sentences on what you're building and why — the CURRENT intent, not the \" +\n        \"originally approved plan (on a recapture, say what changed and why).\\n\" +\n        \"- relates_to_page_id: leave empty for a new initiative. Set it to an existing initiative's page \" +\n        \"id — from hindsight_list_knowledge_pages, or the id this tool returned earlier — to record a \" +\n        \"plan change or an enhancement to it.\\n\\n\" +\n        \"Returns the page id. The page is generated for you — you never format one yourself.\",\n      inputSchema: {\n        title: z.string(),\n        summary: z.string(),\n        relates_to_page_id: z.string().optional(),\n      },\n      annotations: NON_DESTRUCTIVE_WRITE_ANNOTATIONS,\n      handler: guarded(async ({ title, summary, relates_to_page_id }) =>\n        client.captureInitiative({\n          title,\n          summary,\n          relatesToPageId: relates_to_page_id,\n          ...(opts.stampFor ? { stamp: opts.stampFor() } : {}),\n          ...(opts.pageTrigger ? { pageTrigger: opts.pageTrigger } : {}),\n        })\n      ),\n    },\n    {\n      name: \"hindsight_ingest_document\",\n      description:\n        \"Save an external document or a block of durable notes/findings into this repository's \" +\n        \"memory so it informs future recall and pages. Use for design notes, research, or \" +\n        \"reference material you want remembered — not for the conversation you're already in \" +\n        \"(that's captured automatically at session end). This is ALSO the correction mechanism: \" +\n        \"when you verify that a retrieved memory is wrong or outdated, ingest a document titled \" +\n        \"'Correction: <topic>' stating what memory claimed, what is actually true, and the \" +\n        \"evidence — the newer fact supersedes the stale one in future retrieval.\",\n      inputSchema: { title: z.string(), content: z.string() },\n      annotations: NON_DESTRUCTIVE_WRITE_ANNOTATIONS,\n      handler: guarded(async ({ title, content }) => {\n        const slug = title\n          .toLowerCase()\n          .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, \"-\")\n          .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, \"\");\n        // ASCII-only slugs erased non-Latin titles (or shared the \"doc\" fallback),\n        // overwriting unrelated documents. Hash the original title, not its content,\n        // so re-ingestion still updates it; \"--\" cannot occur in a legacy slug.\n        const docId =\n          /[^\\x00-\\x7f]/.test(title) || !slug\n            ? `${slug || \"doc\"}--${createHash(\"sha256\").update(title).digest(\"hex\")}`\n            : slug;\n        const stamp = opts.stampFor?.();\n        const metadata = {\n          ...stamp?.metadata,\n          ...(opts.harness ? { harness: opts.harness } : {}),\n        };\n        await client.retain(\n          content,\n          \"ingested document\",\n          docId,\n          [\n            ...new Set([\n              ...(stamp?.tags ?? []),\n              \"source:upload\",\n              ...(opts.harness ? [`harness:${opts.harness}`] : []),\n            ]),\n          ],\n          \"document\",\n          Object.keys(metadata).length ? { metadata } : {}\n        );\n        return { ok: true, doc_id: docId };\n      }),\n    },\n  ];\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "hindsight-integrations/coding-agents/src/core/retain-cursor.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * How much of a live session has already been written to its `conversation:<id>` document.\n *\n * Without a cursor every write-back re-uploads the WHOLE conversation: a long session re-sends the\n * entire transcript on every Stop (and every N turns under the persistent-plugin runtime), which is\n * what makes a runaway session unretainable rather than merely large. With one, a retain sends only\n * the turns added since the last successful write, using the server's `update_mode: \"append\"`.\n *\n * Append is only correct while our view of the document matches the server's, so this deliberately\n * falls back to a FULL REPLACE — which is idempotent by construction and therefore always safe —\n * whenever that cannot be established:\n *\n *   - no cursor          first write-back of the session, or the cache was evicted.\n *   - fingerprint drift  the transcript was REWRITTEN rather than extended (an edited or redacted\n *                        turn, a truncated/rotated rollout), so what we already sent is no longer a\n *                        prefix of what we hold and an append would splice two conversations.\n *                        NOT Claude Code compaction, which this used to cite: that appends a\n *                        summary record and leaves every earlier record in place (#3379), so the\n *                        prefix stays intact and the append path keeps working.\n *                        NOR a session that moved to a NEW transcript FILE (Codex writes a\n *                        continuation rollout under the same session id, #4493): nothing was\n *                        rewritten there, the earlier turns simply live in the earlier file, so\n *                        that case appends the new file whole instead of replacing the document\n *                        with it — see `paths` below.\n *   - dirty              a REPLACE was started and not confirmed. There is nothing worth replaying\n *                        (another replace re-establishes the same truth from the same transcript),\n *                        so the next write-back simply replaces again.\n *   - failed op          a write the server accepted whose operation later FAILED (see `ops`): its\n *                        turns never reached the document, so appending after them leaves a gap.\n *\n * An APPEND that fails does NOT fall back to replace, because that fallback is what made a single\n * outage cost a full re-extraction on every subsequent Stop for the life of the session (#3989).\n * Its bytes are buffered in `pending` instead and replayed on the next write-back, unchanged and\n * under their original operation id — so a write the server actually committed is collapsed into\n * that same operation rather than appending the turns twice, which is the only thing appending onto\n * an unknown state could otherwise get wrong. Refetching here (rather than replaying a\n   * cached list) is the whole point — the cached one predates the reply.\n   *\n   * Cadence is deliberately bypassed: idle means \"there may be nothing after this\", so a pending\n   * turn must not wait for a threshold it will never reach.\n   */\n  async onSessionIdle(sessionId: string): Promise<void> {\n    if (process.env.HINDSIGHT_DISABLE_HOOKS) return; // anti-recursion (see seedIfCold)\n    if (!sessionId || !this.fetchTranscript) return;\n    let turns: TransportTurn[];\n    try {\n      turns = await this.fetchTranscript(sessionId);\n    } catch (e) {\n      diag(this.harness, \"idle_fetch_failed\", {\n        error: describeError(e),\n        session: sessionId,\n      });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!turns.length) return;\n    this.recordUsage(sessionId, turns, true); // idle: the reply is in\n    if (!this.writeBackEnabled) return; // usage above is local and recorded regardless (#5391)\n    const st = this.stateFor(sessionId);\n    // idle can fire more than once for one exchange (and again on a session with no new activity);\n    // only retain when this transcript actually grew past what we last wrote.\n    if (turns.length <= st.retainedTurns) return;\n    st.retainedTurns = turns.length;\n    this.retain(sessionId, turns, st.startTs, \"idle\");\n  }\n\n  private recordUsage(sessionId: string, turns: TransportTurn[], lastTurnComplete: boolean): void {\n    recordUsage({\n      harness: this.harness,\n      sessionId,\n      bankId: this.bankId,\n      turns,\n      cursors: this.usageCursors,\n      lastTurnComplete,\n      // No `reviseLastTurn` here, unlike the hook path: this runtime never records a turn before its\n      // reply exists. `onTranscript` is handed `false` while the host is still building the request,\n      // which holds the turn back, and `onSessionIdle` refetches a transcript that includes the\n      // reply before recording it.\n    });\n  }\n\n  private stateFor(sessionId: string): {\n    startTs: string;\n    retainedTurns: number;\n  } {\n    let st = this.sessionState.get(sessionId);\n    if (!st) {\n      st = { startTs: new Date().toISOString(), retainedTurns: 0 };\n      this.sessionState.set(sessionId, st);\n    }\n    return st;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Wait for every write-back still in flight, at most `timeoutMs`. Write-backs stay fire-and-forget\n   * so a turn never blocks on the network; a host that announces its exit (pi's `session_shutdown`)\n   * calls this so the session's final retain is not dropped with the process (#5081). Bounded so a\n   * stalled server cannot hold the host's exit open. Never throws.\n   */\n  async flush(timeoutMs = FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<void> {\n    if (!this.inFlight.size) return;\n    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;\n    await Promise.race([\n      Promise.all(this.inFlight),\n      new Promise<void>((r) => {\n        timer = setTimeout(r, timeoutMs);\n      }),\n    ]);\n    clearTimeout(timer);\n  }\n\n  /** Fire-and-forget upsert of the session transcript; never throws into the host. */\n  private retain(\n    sessionId: string,\n    turns: TransportTurn[],\n    startTs: string,\n    trigger = \"turn\"\n  ): void {\n    const t0 = Date.now();\n    // Daemon mode: the write path is the last chance to get a daemon up — the Stop-hook role, for\n    // hosts that have no Stop hook. A daemon that died mid-session would otherwise take the whole\n    // exchange with it. The wait sits INSIDE the fire-and-forget chain, so\n    // unlike the Stop hook it costs the host nothing: this call already returns before the retain\n    // does. Deliberately not gated on the result — retain proceeds either way, so an unreachable\n    // daemon produces the same `retain_failed` diagnostic as an unreachable Cloud server.\n    const write = ensureDaemon(this.cfg, this.harness, { waitMs: DAEMON_WAIT_RETAIN_MS })\n      .then(() =>\n        retainLiveSession(this.client, sessionId, turns, startTs, this.harness, {\n          cursors: this.cursors,\n          stamp: buildRetainStamp(this.cfg, {\n            directory: this.projectDir,\n            harness: this.harness,\n            bankId: this.bankId,\n            sessionId,\n          }),\n        })\n      )\n      .then(() =>\n        diag(this.harness, \"retain_ok\", {\n          ms: Date.now() - t0,\n          turns: turns.length,\n          session: sessionId,\n          trigger,\n        })\n      )\n      .catch((e) =>\n        diag(this.harness, \"retain_failed\", {\n          ms: Date.now() - t0,\n          error: describeError(e),\n          session: sessionId,\n          trigger,\n        })\n      );\n    this.inFlight.add(write);\n    void write.finally(() => this.inFlight.delete(write));\n  }\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "hindsight-integrations/coding-agents/src/core/seed.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Per-bank seed-consent state, for the auto-seed flow (Task 10).\n *\n * (Cold-repo detection itself lives in core/session-start.ts, which needs a tri-state result —\n * cold / warm / server-unreachable — that a plain boolean can't express.)\n *\n * Fail-safe throughout: state read/write never throws — a corrupt or unwritable state file must\n * not break the hook.\n */\nimport { spawn as realSpawn } from \"node:child_process\";\nimport { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport { dirname, join } from \"node:path\";\nimport { fileURLToPath } from \"node:url\";\n\nexport const DEFAULT_SEED_LIMIT = 300;\n\n/** Spawn a DETACHED background run of the deepen engine for `repoDir`. Idempotent server-side\n *  (per-bank lock + dedup by document id), so firing it every session start is safe — each run does\n *  only the missing work (cold seed, new conversations, the next diff-deepening batch). Fire-and-forget:\n *  the child outlives this process; extraction is server-side/async so nothing here blocks. Never throws. */\nexport function startBackgroundSeed(\n  repoDir: string,\n  opts: { limit?: number; harness?: string; enginePath?: string; spawn?: typeof realSpawn } = {}\n): void {\n  try {\n    const spawnFn = opts.spawn ?? realSpawn;\n    const enginePath =\n      opts.enginePath ?? join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), \"deepen.js\");\n    const limit = opts.limit ?? DEFAULT_SEED_LIMIT;\n    // The engine writes the leveled plugin.log itself (core/log.ts), so the child's stdio can be\n    // fully detached — no fd redirect to manage.\n    const child = spawnFn(\n      \"node\",\n      [\n        enginePath,\n        \"--repo\",\n        repoDir,\n        \"--gitlog-limit\",\n        String(limit),\n        ...(opts.harness ? [\"--harness\", opts.harness] : []),\n      ],\n      {\n        detached: true,\n        stdio: \"ignore\",\n        windowsHide: true,\n      }\n    );\n    // spawn() failures (ENOENT/EACCES/fd exhaustion/sandboxed environments) often arrive\n    // ASYNCHRONOUSLY as an 'error' event on the child, not as a synchronous throw — an\n    // unhandled 'error' event would crash the caller. Swallow it: fire-and-forget best-effort.\n    child.on(\"error\", () => {});\n    child.unref();\n  } catch {\n    /* best-effort: a failed spawn must not break the caller */\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface SeedControlResult {\n  ok: boolean;\n  message: string;\n}\n\n/** Execute a seed-control command. Pure-ish: bank + connection are passed in; spawn + stateDir injectable. */\nexport function seedControl(\n  command: string,\n  args: {\n    repo: string;\n    bankId: string;\n    limit?: number;\n    spawn?: typeof realSpawn;\n  }\n): SeedControlResult {\n  if (command === \"seed\") {\n    startBackgroundSeed(args.repo, { limit: args.limit, spawn: args.spawn });\n    return {\n      ok: true,\n      message: `🧠 Hindsight is learning this repo → memory bank “${args.bankId}”`,\n    };\n  }\n  return { ok: false, message: \"usage: hindsight-seed seed --repo <dir>\" };\n}\n"
