      "path": "hindsight-integrations/coding-agents/src/core/session-start.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Shared `SessionStart` lifecycle: deterministically auto-seeds a cold repo's bank from its git\n * history (in the background, non-blocking), keeps warm banks deepening on every start, and\n * injects a short visible note plus the live\n * knowledge-page roster + guidance preamble that tells the agent to consult the repo's pages.\n *\n * Earlier design injected an instruction asking the AGENT to pose a y/n question to the user and\n * then run a seed command itself. Live testing showed that doesn't work: the model surfaces the\n * question, then plows ahead with the user's actual task and never runs the command — so nothing\n * ever seeds. Fix: the hook does the seeding itself. There is nothing left for the agent to decide\n * or execute for seeding, so no shell command (and no shell-escaping) is needed anymore.\n *\n * Tri-state cold check: a boolean \"is it cold?\" would collapse \"cold\" and \"server unreachable\"\n * into the same outcome, which is wrong here — a transient outage must not get treated the same\n * as \"already seeded\" and silently suppress seeding forever. So `buildSessionStartContext` calls\n * `client.listDocumentIds` directly so it can tell the three cases apart:\n *   - throws (server unreachable)      -> no seed, no state written  (try again next session)\n *   - non-empty set (warm/pre-seeded)  -> no seed, seededAt written  (remember, skip enumerating)\n *   - empty set (cold)                 -> start the background seed, seededAt written, note added\n * \"Empty\" means no git documents AND no survey-baseline marker: under `gitIngest: \"none\"` no git\n * document is ever written, and the markers are what show the repo was already surveyed (#5124).\n */\nimport { gitHeadSha, gitLogIsCurrent, hasGitHistory, commitsSince } from \"./git\";\nimport { DEEPEN_DIFF_TARGET } from \"./status\";\nimport { startBackgroundSeed } from \"./seed\";\nimport { maybeAutoUpdate } from \"./auto-update\";\nimport { syncCompanionSkill } from \"./skill-sync\";\nimport { SURVEY_DOC_IDS, startCodebaseSurvey, type SurveyHarness } from \"./survey\";\nimport { applyBankConfig, loadConfig } from \"./config\";\nimport { DAEMON_WAIT_SESSION_START_MS, ensureDaemon } from \"./daemon\";\nimport type { Config } from \"./config\";\nimport { deriveBankIdOrSkip } from \"./bank\";\nimport { brandWord } from \"./brand\";\nimport { diag, readHookEvent } from \"./diag\";\nimport { setLogLevel } from \"./log\";\nimport { parsePageList, buildKnowledgePreamble, type PageRef } from \"./knowledge-injection\";\nimport type { ClientOpts, RetainOpts } from \"./hindsight\";\nimport { buildRetainStamp } from \"./retain-stamp\";\nimport { detectLegacyClaudePlugin, legacyClaudePluginWarning } from \"./legacy\";\nimport { HindsightClient } from \"./hindsight\";\nimport {\n  sessionCacheFile,\n  sessionRootDir,\n  stashPendingContext,\n  writeSessionCache,\n} from \"./session-cache\";\n\n/** Minimal client shape `buildSessionStartContext` needs. */\ninterface SeedContextClient {\n  listDocumentIds(tag: string, tagsMatch?: \"all\" | \"all_strict\"): Promise<Set<string>>;\n  // Optional: lets the git note see a git-log document written at a commit HEAD is behind\n  // (gitLogIsCurrent). The minimal test clients omit it and keep the exact-HEAD check.\n  documentTags?(documentId: string): Promise<string[] | undefined>;\n  listPages(): Promise<unknown>;\n  // Optional: whether the bank holds any document at all. Without it the first-prompt reflect is\n  // never deferred — only a confirmed-empty bank is.\n  hasDocuments?(): Promise<boolean>;\n  knowledgePagesSupported?: boolean;\n  // Optional: used to write the survey-baseline marker (Option A). HindsightClient has it; the\n  // minimal test clients omit it, and the baseline write guards on its presence.\n  retain?(\n    content: string,\n    context: string,\n    documentId: string,\n    tags: string[],\n    strategy: string,\n    opts?: RetainOpts\n  ): Promise<void>;\n}\n\n/**\n * The session banner: one line — the gradient \"Hindsight\" wordmark (same colors as the API\n * server's banner) plus the repo's bank. Shown on EVERY session start; \"learning\" on a cold\n * repo (first ingest running), \"remembering\" once the bank is warm.\n */\nexport function buildSeedBanner(bankId: string, cold = true, gitNote?: string): string {\n  // Two lines: what Hindsight DOES for this repo (value, not mechanism), then where the memory\n  // lives + sync state. The brand word leads line 1 so the host TUI's message prefix lands there.\n  const headline = cold\n    ? `${brandWord()} is learning this repo — ingesting its decisions, conventions and history`\n    : `${brandWord()} is tracking the decisions, conventions and history of this repo`;\n  const details = `  ↳ memory bank “${bankId}”` + (gitNote ? ` · ${gitNote}` : \"\");\n  return `${headline}\\n${details}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * One-phrase git-sync state for the banner (the syncStatus contract, condensed): whether the bank\n * is current with the repo's commits. Cheap — reuses the cold-check's doc-id set plus ONE tag query\n * (gitlog-head:<sha>, the freshness marker the deepen engine maintains), and one read of that tag\n * when HEAD is not the commit it names. Same check as the deepen engine's (gitLogIsCurrent), so the\n * banner never promises a catch-up the engine will skip. Returns undefined when there's nothing\n * meaningful to say (gitIngest off, no git, cold bank — \"learning\" already covers it).\n */\nasync function gitSyncNote(args: {\n  client: SeedContextClient;\n  cwd: string;\n  gitIds: Set<string>;\n  mode: \"message\" | \"full\" | \"none\";\n  cold: boolean;\n}): Promise<string | undefined> {\n  const { client, cwd, gitIds, mode, cold } = args;\n  if (mode === \"none\" || cold) return undefined;\n  const head = gitHeadSha(cwd);\n  if (!head) return undefined;\n  const gitlogCurrent = await gitLogIsCurrent(client, cwd, head).catch(() => undefined);\n  if (gitlogCurrent === undefined) return undefined; // server hiccup: say nothing rather than guess\n  if (mode === \"message\") return gitlogCurrent ? \"git in sync\" : \"catching up on new commits\";\n  // full: deepening progress = per-commit docs vs the recent-history target\n  const deepened = [...gitIds].filter((id) => id.startsWith(\"git:\")).length;\n  let target = DEEPEN_DIFF_TARGET;\n  try {\n    const { execFileSync } = await import(\"node:child_process\");\n    const n = Number(\n      execFileSync(\"git\", [\"-C\", cwd, \"rev-list\", \"--count\", \"HEAD\"], {\n        encoding: \"utf8\",\n        windowsHide: true,\n        stdio: [\"ignore\", \"pipe\", \"pipe\"], // do not corrupt the host banner on a late git failure\n      }).trim()\n    );\n    if (n > 0) target = Math.min(DEEPEN_DIFF_TARGET, n);\n  } catch {\n    /* keep the default target */\n  }\n  return gitlogCurrent && deepened >= target\n    ? \"git in sync\"\n    : `syncing git history (${Math.min(deepened, target)}/${target})`;\n}\n\n/** Split SessionStart output: `systemMessage` renders in the terminal (user-visible);\n *  `additionalContext` is injected into the model's context only. */\nexport interface SessionStartOutput {\n  systemMessage?: string;\n  additionalContext?: string;\n  /** Internal lifecycle signal: defer one auto-reflect while a new bank gains useful content. */\n  deferInitialReflect?: boolean;\n}\n\n/** Host-specific adapter for the shared SessionStart core. Claude and Codex use the\n * Claude-compatible envelope; Cursor's native hooks require snake-case `additional_context`. */\nexport interface SessionStartHookSpec {\n  harness: string;\n  parse(event: Record<string, unknown>): { cwd?: string; sessionId?: string };\n  /** Optional event gate, evaluated before config loading: false makes the hook a silent no-op. */\n  accept?(event: Record<string, unknown>): boolean;\n  emit(output: SessionStartOutput): unknown;\n  /** The host drops SessionStart context (Grok Build, #5467): stash it for the session's first tool\n   *  hook instead — see HookSpec.toolHook. */\n  deferContextToToolHook?: boolean;\n  /** Optional per-repo host registration, run once memory is confirmed LIVE for the repo (after\n   *  bank derivation and the opt-in/`disabled` gates). Returns an optional user-facing banner\n   *  hint (registration maintenance is host business, its absence a host problem) and must never\n   *  throw. TraeCode uses this to keep `<repo>/.trae/mcp.json` registering its MCP server and to\n   *  nudge when the workspace-MCP gate hides it (core/traecode-mcp.ts). */\n  ensureMcpRegistration?: (cwd: string) => string | undefined;\n}\n\n/**\n * Build this session's additionalContext: (maybe) kick off a background auto-seed of a cold repo\n * and (always, unless the hook is disabled) append the knowledge-page bank mission. See module doc\n * for the tri-state cold check. Never throws.\n */\nexport async function buildSessionStartContext(args: {\n  cwd: string;\n  /** Where the session started — see `sessionRootDir`. Same as `cwd` on a fresh session; they\n   *  differ on a resume, where the bank was resolved from the ORIGINAL root. */\n  sessionRoot?: string;\n  bankId: string;\n  cfg: Config;\n  client: SeedContextClient;\n  harness?: string;\n  stateDir?: string;\n  hasGit?: (dir: string) => boolean;\n  startSeed?: (repoDir: string, opts?: { limit?: number; harness?: string }) => void;\n  startSurvey?: typeof startCodebaseSurvey;\n  headSha?: (dir: string) => string | null;\n  commitsSince?: (dir: string, sinceSha: string) => number | null;\n  /** Registry key of the old Claude Code plugin still active for `cwd`; defaults to reading\n   *  Claude's plugin files, and only for the claude-code harness. */\n  detectLegacyPlugin?: (cwd: string) => string | undefined;\n}): Promise<SessionStartOutput> {\n  const { cwd, bankId, cfg, client, stateDir } = args;\n  const t0 = Date.now();\n  let cold: boolean | undefined; // undefined = not checked (autoSeed off / non-git / unreachable)\n  let gitDocIds: Set<string> | undefined; // the cold-check's doc set, reused by the banner's git note\n  let bankEmpty = false; // true only when the server confirmed the bank holds no documents\n  const harness = args.harness ?? \"claude-code\";\n  const hasGit = args.hasGit ?? hasGitHistory;\n  const startSeed = args.startSeed ?? startBackgroundSeed;\n  const startSurvey = args.startSurvey ?? startCodebaseSurvey;\n  const resolveHeadSha = args.headSha ?? gitHeadSha;\n  const countCommitsSince = args.commitsSince ?? commitsSince;\n  // sessionRoot as well as cwd, so a stamped {gitProject} names the project the bank id does.\n  const retainStamp = () =>\n    buildRetainStamp(cfg, { directory: cwd, sessionRoot: args.sessionRoot, harness, bankId });\n\n  // Codebase-survey baseline (Option A): the bank is the only state, so the HEAD at the last survey\n  // is recorded IN the bank as a tiny `survey-baseline:<sha>` marker doc (tag source:survey-baseline;\n  // content = the bare sha so extraction yields no facts), mirroring the deepen engine's gitlog-head\n  // marker. The commit-count re-survey reads these back by tag.\n  const SURVEY_BASELINE_TAG = \"source:survey-baseline\";\n  const SURVEY_BASELINE_PREFIX = \"survey-baseline:\";\n  const recordSurveyBaseline = (sha: string): void => {\n    if (!client.retain) return; // minimal client (some tests) — nothing to record\n    try {\n      const stamp = retainStamp();\n      const content =\n        `🛰️ Hindsight is researching this codebase — survey started at commit ${sha.slice(0, 12)}. ` +\n        `(Internal marker: no memories are extracted from this document.)`;\n      const tags = [...new Set([...stamp.tags, SURVEY_BASELINE_TAG])];\n      // Fire-and-forget; Promise.resolve tolerates a non-Promise return (e.g. a test spy).\n      const retained = client.retain(\n        content,\n        \"hindsight codebase-survey baseline\",\n        `${SURVEY_BASELINE_PREFIX}${sha}`,\n        tags,\n        \"survey\",\n        // `retain` only sets metadata when it is truthy, so an empty stamp sends none.\n        { metadata: Object.keys(stamp.metadata).length ? stamp.metadata : undefined }\n      );\n      void Promise.resolve(retained).catch(() => {});\n    } catch {\n      /* best-effort — a failed baseline write never breaks SessionStart */\n    }\n  };\n\n  // The banner is USER-FACING and must ride `systemMessage` (the only hook field Claude Code\n  // renders in the terminal); `additionalContext` is model-only and would show the human nothing.\n  // The knowledge preamble is model context and stays in `additionalContext`.\n  let systemMessage: string | undefined;\n\n  if (cfg.autoSeed !== false) {\n    if (hasGit(cwd)) {\n      // The LIVE bank is the ONLY state (cold-check-wins): delete the bank and the next session is\n      // a true first-open — no client-side flags can contradict it. Opting out of memory is the\n      // `disabled` config field (global or per-harness), not a hidden state file.\n      {\n        let docIds: Set<string> | undefined;\n        try {\n          docIds = await client.listDocumentIds(\"source:git\", \"all_strict\");\n        } catch {\n          docIds = undefined; // server unreachable: transient — do nothing, try again next session\n        }\n\n        // No git documents is not the whole story: under `gitIngest: \"none\"` none are ever\n        // written, so a bank an earlier session already surveyed still reads as cold and every\n        // session would launch another survey (#5124). Its survey-baseline markers say otherwise\n        // — the same evidence the warm branch below reads. An unreadable marker list keeps the\n        // git-only answer.\n        let baselines: Set<string> | undefined;\n        if (docIds?.size === 0) {\n          baselines = await client\n            .listDocumentIds(SURVEY_BASELINE_TAG, \"all_strict\")\n            .catch(() => undefined);\n        }\n        cold = docIds !== undefined ? docIds.size === 0 && !baselines?.size : undefined;\n        gitDocIds = docIds;\n        // Only a CONFIRMED-empty bank defers the first-prompt reflect. A cold repo can sit in a\n        // bank that already holds memories (a shared bank, imported conversations), and a failed\n        // or missing probe proves nothing (#5209). Probed before the seed and the survey baseline\n        // below write their first documents.\n        if (cold === true && client.hasDocuments) {\n          bankEmpty = await client.hasDocuments().then(\n            (has) => !has,\n            () => false\n          );\n        }\n        if (docIds !== undefined) {\n          // ALWAYS fire the background deepen engine when the server is reachable — it is\n          // idempotent (per-bank lock, dedup by document id) and each run does only the missing\n          // work: cold seed, newly appeared conversations, the next per-commit diff batch. The\n          // one-time extras stay cold-gated below.\n          // Pass the ASKING harness through: without it deepen.js falls back to the config\n          // loader's harness default and misfiles this session's survey + git history into the\n          // wrong bank (e.g. `opencode::<project>` for a claude-code session). See #3247.\n          startSeed(cwd, { limit: cfg.seedLimit, harness });\n          // Cold iff the bank has zero source:git docs and no survey baseline (an undefined result\n          // — server error — is NOT treated as cold; we never surveyed/noted on an unconfirmed-empty\n          // bank).\n          if (cold) {\n            if (cfg.codebaseSurvey !== false) {\n              // Run the survey under the current harness's own CLI (falls back to any available agent).\n              const sha = resolveHeadSha(cwd);\n              const started = await startSurvey(cwd, {\n                harness: harness as SurveyHarness,\n                model: cfg.surveyModel,\n                budgetUsd: cfg.surveyBudgetUsd,\n                sha: sha ?? undefined,\n              });\n              if (started && sha) recordSurveyBaseline(sha);\n            }\n            diag(harness, \"seed_started\", { bank: bankId });\n          } else if (cfg.codebaseSurvey !== false && cfg.surveyRefreshCommits > 0) {\n            // WARM bank: re-run the survey once enough commits have accrued since the last one, so\n            // structural pages track an evolving architecture. Branch-robust: read the\n            // survey-baseline:<sha> markers and take the MIN reachable `sha..HEAD` count (= the most\n            // recent survey that's an ancestor of HEAD; dead-branch/rebased markers are unreachable →\n            // ignored). No reachable baseline yet (pre-feature bank, or all markers gone) => record\n            // HEAD as the baseline WITHOUT surveying (no surprise spend).\n            const sha = resolveHeadSha(cwd);\n            if (sha) {\n              const markers =\n                baselines ??\n                (await client\n                  .listDocumentIds(SURVEY_BASELINE_TAG, \"all_strict\")\n                  .catch(() => new Set<string>()));\n              const counts: number[] = [];\n              for (const id of markers) {\n                if (!id.startsWith(SURVEY_BASELINE_PREFIX)) continue;\n                const n = countCommitsSince(cwd, id.slice(SURVEY_BASELINE_PREFIX.length));\n                if (n !== null) counts.push(n);\n              }\n              const sinceLast = counts.length ? Math.min(...counts) : null;\n              // A baseline without FINDINGS means the surveyed agent died before ingesting (no\n              // CLI on PATH, budget kill) — the marker alone must not suppress retries forever.\n              const uploads = await client\n                .listDocumentIds(\"source:upload\", \"all_strict\")\n                .catch(() => new Set<string>());\n              const findingsAbsent =\n                counts.length > 0 && !SURVEY_DOC_IDS.some((id) => uploads.has(id));\n              if ((sinceLast !== null && sinceLast >= cfg.surveyRefreshCommits) || findingsAbsent) {\n                const started = await startSurvey(cwd, {\n                  harness: harness as SurveyHarness,\n                  model: cfg.surveyModel,\n                  budgetUsd: cfg.surveyBudgetUsd,\n                  sha,\n                });\n                if (started) {\n                  recordSurveyBaseline(sha);\n                  diag(harness, \"survey_refresh\", {\n                    bank: bankId,\n                    commits: sinceLast,\n                    retry: findingsAbsent,\n                  });\n                }\n              } else if (sinceLast === null) {\n                recordSurveyBaseline(sha); // first baseline, or reset after a rebase — no survey\n              }\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  let pages: PageRef[] = [];\n  try {\n    pages = parsePageList(await client.listPages());\n  } catch {\n    if (client.knowledgePagesSupported === false) {\n      diag(harness, \"knowledge_pages_unavailable\", { bank: bankId });\n    }\n    /* fail-open preamble */\n  }\n  const additionalContext = buildKnowledgePreamble(pages, {\n    reflectOnNewGoals: cfg.autoInject !== \"reflect\",\n    extra: cfg.toolGuideExtra,\n  });\n  // An empty page roster is NOT an empty bank: a bank with memories and no pages still answers a\n  // reflect (#5209), so only the confirmed-empty probe above defers it.\n  const deferInitialReflect = bankEmpty;\n\n  // The banner shows on EVERY session — Hindsight's presence is part of the product, not a\n  // one-time setup note. Wording tracks the bank state: cold = \"learning\", else \"remembering\";\n  // warm banners also condense the syncStatus contract into a git-sync phrase.\n  let gitNote: string | undefined;\n  if (gitDocIds) {\n    gitNote = await gitSyncNote({\n      client,\n      cwd,\n      gitIds: gitDocIds,\n      mode: cfg.gitIngest,\n      cold: cold === true,\n    }).catch(() => undefined);\n  }\n  systemMessage = buildSeedBanner(bankId, cold === true, gitNote);\n\n  // The old per-agent plugin keeps running next to this one until the user removes it — say so\n  // where they will see it. Only Claude Code had that plugin.\n  const detectLegacy =\n    args.detectLegacyPlugin ?? (harness === \"claude-code\" ? detectLegacyClaudePlugin : undefined);\n  const legacyPlugin = detectLegacy?.(cwd);\n  if (legacyPlugin) {\n    systemMessage += `\\n${legacyClaudePluginWarning(legacyPlugin)}`;\n    diag(harness, \"legacy_plugin_active\", { plugin: legacyPlugin });\n  }\n\n  // ALWAYS record the session start (warm sessions used to log nothing — undebuggable).\n  diag(harness, \"session_start\", { bank: bankId, cold, pages: pages.length, ms: Date.now() - t0 });\n\n  return { systemMessage, additionalContext, deferInitialReflect };\n}\n\n/** Run one SessionStart hook invocation: stdin event in, (maybe) an additionalContext object on stdout. */\nexport async function runSessionStartHook(\n  spec: SessionStartHookSpec,\n  makeClient: (opts: ClientOpts) => SeedContextClient = (o) => new HindsightClient(o)\n): Promise<void> {\n  // Anti-recursion: the codebase survey's own headless claude session (core/survey.ts) sets this\n  // so its hooks are a no-op — it must not re-seed/re-survey its own survey session.\n  if (process.env.HINDSIGHT_DISABLE_HOOKS) return;\n\n  // Whole-body try/catch (unlike runHook/runRetainHook, which only guard individual steps): a\n  // throw here happens during session bootstrap, before the agent has done anything — more\n  // disruptive than a failure mid-prompt — so nothing in this function may ever escape it.\n  try {\n    const ev = readHookEvent(spec.harness);\n    if (!ev) return;\n    if (spec.accept && !spec.accept(ev)) return;\n    const { harness } = spec;\n    const { cwd: rawCwd, sessionId } = spec.parse(ev);\n    const cwd = rawCwd || process.cwd();\n\n    let cfg = loadConfig({ harness });\n    setLogLevel(cfg.logLevel);\n    syncCompanionSkill(harness); // keep the installed skill current with the package version\n    if (cfg.disabled) return;\n    // …and keep the package itself current. AFTER the disabled check, unlike the skill sync above:\n    // `disabled` means an inert plugin, and a network call plus a background npm install is not\n    // inert. It also keeps the two harness families symmetric — the plugin hosts never construct a\n    // RuntimeCore when disabled (harness/plugin-entry.ts), so they already skip this.\n    // Detached and rate-limited to once a day; the update lands for the NEXT session.\n    void maybeAutoUpdate(cfg);\n\n    // Recorded HERE, on the session's first hook, so every later hook of this session resolves the\n    // same bank however far the agent navigates (#3563).\n    const sessionRoot = sessionRootDir(harness, sessionId, cwd);\n    const derived = deriveBankIdOrSkip(cfg, cwd, harness, sessionRoot);\n    if (derived === null) return; // repository unidentifiable: no bank, no seed, no injection\n    const resolved = applyBankConfig(cfg, derived, cwd);\n    cfg = resolved.cfg;\n    const bankId = resolved.bankId;\n    if (cfg.disabled) return; // per-bank opt-out (banks.<id> override)\n    // Memory is live HERE — the one point where registering the host's per-repo MCP access is\n    // correct: the caller of an opt-out repo must not gain a config file it never asked for.\n    const mcpHint = spec.ensureMcpRegistration?.(cwd);\n    // Daemon mode: warm it up now, before the user has typed anything. The start itself is\n    // detached; we wait only briefly, so an already-running daemon is adopted immediately while a\n    // cold one keeps coming up in the background and is picked up by a later turn.\n    await ensureDaemon(cfg, harness, { waitMs: DAEMON_WAIT_SESSION_START_MS });\n    const client = makeClient({\n      apiUrl: cfg.apiUrl,\n      apiToken: cfg.apiToken,\n      bank: bankId,\n      maxParallelRetains: cfg.maxParallelRetains,\n      observationScopes: cfg.observationScopes,\n    });\n\n    const out = await buildSessionStartContext({ cwd, sessionRoot, bankId, cfg, client, harness });\n    // The registration's banner hint (e.g. TraeCode's workspace-MCP gate) rides the same\n    // user-facing message as the legacy-plugin warning — the banner is the only visible channel.\n    if (mcpHint)\n      out.systemMessage = out.systemMessage ? `${out.systemMessage}\\n${mcpHint}` : mcpHint;\n    if (out.deferInitialReflect && sessionId) {\n      writeSessionCache(sessionCacheFile(harness, sessionId), { deferInitialReflect: true });\n    }\n    if (spec.deferContextToToolHook && out.additionalContext && sessionId) {\n      stashPendingContext(harness, sessionId, out.additionalContext);\n      out.additionalContext = undefined;\n    }\n    // The lifecycle computes one host-neutral output; the registry owns each host's wire schema.\n    const payload = spec.emit(out);\n    if (out.systemMessage || out.additionalContext) {\n      process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(payload));\n    }\n  } catch {\n    /* SessionStart must never throw and break the session */\n  }\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "hindsight-integrations/coding-agents/src/core/transcript-dsh.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * DeepSeek Harness (dsh) transcript normalizer.\n *\n * dsh keeps a session as an append-only log of typed `SessionEvent`s rather than a chat array, and\n * a plugin reads that log straight off the live session (`snapshotEvents()`) — so this is a pure\n * function over those events, like the opencode normalizer, not a file reader. The SAME event\n * vocabulary is what dsh persists to disk, so the backfill reader (core/history.ts) feeds this\n * exact function.\n *\n * Only three of the ~30 event types carry conversation:\n *   - `user/message`      surface, a UserMessage — the human prompt OR an injected plugin context\n *   - `assistant/message` surface, the assembled reply for one step\n *   - `tool/call`         log-only, the model's tool invocation (rendered as a compact action turn)\n * `tool/result` is deliberately skipped: its payload is raw tool output, which the shared\n * `actionLine` convention keeps out of the bank (see transcript-util.ts).\n *\n * A `user/message` is only kept when its source is an actual HUMAN (`source.kind === 'user'`).\n * dsh delivers plugin context — its own runtime-context snapshots, the skill catalog, file-change\n * notices, and OUR recalled memories — as user-role messages on the same surface, and retaining\n * those would file machine scaffolding as if the user had said it (and, for our own block, feed\n * recalled memory straight back into the next extraction). The tag-based `stripInjectedMemory`\n * still runs on what remains, for text that arrived inside a genuine prompt.\n */\nimport type { TransportTurn } from \"./chat\";\nimport { actionLine, stripInjectedMemory } from \"./transcript-util\";\n\n/**\n * The Cordis plugin name. Messages this integration injects carry `source.kind: 'plugin:hindsight'`\n * (the V4 producer-owned kind; V3 logs recorded `kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'hindsight'`), so an\n * injected block is identifiable in a session log even though the `kind: 'user'` filter below\n * already keeps it (and every other plugin's context) out of a retain.\n */\nexport const HINDSIGHT_PLUGIN = \"hindsight\";\n\n/** Structural subset of a dsh ContentBlock (text is the only kind that carries prose). */\ninterface DshContentBlock {\n  type?: string;\n  text?: string;\n}\n\n/** Structural subset of a dsh Message ({ id, role, content, source }). */\ninterface DshMessage {\n  role?: string;\n  content?: DshContentBlock[];\n  source?: { kind?: string; plugin?: string };\n}\n\n/** Structural subset of a dsh SessionEvent. `data` is the per-type payload. */\nexport interface DshSessionEvent {\n  type?: string;\n  time?: number;\n  data?: unknown;\n}\n\n/** Join a message's text blocks; reasoning/image/tool blocks carry no durable prose. */\nfunction textOf(message: DshMessage): string {\n  return (message.content || [])\n    .filter((block) => block?.type === \"text\" && typeof block.text === \"string\")\n    .map((block) => block.text!)\n    .join(\"\\n\")\n    .trim();\n}\n\n/** dsh stamps epoch milliseconds on every event; absent only on malformed input. */\nfunction stampOf(event: DshSessionEvent): { timestamp?: string } {\n  return typeof event.time === \"number\" ? { timestamp: new Date(event.time).toISOString() } : {};\n}\n\n/**\n * Normalize a dsh session event log into transcript turns: user/assistant prose plus compact\n * `role:\"action\"` turns for tool calls. Never throws on malformed entries.\n */\nexport function readDshEvents(events: readonly DshSessionEvent[]): TransportTurn[] {\n  const turns: TransportTurn[] = [];\n  for (const event of events || []) {\n    if (!event || typeof event !== \"object\") continue;\n    const stamp = stampOf(event);\n    if (event.type === \"user/message\") {\n      const message = event.data as DshMessage | undefined;\n      if (!message || message.source?.kind !== \"user\") continue;\n      const text = stripInjectedMemory(textOf(message)).trim();\n      if (text) turns.push({ role: \"user\", content: text, ...stamp });\n    } else if (event.type === \"assistant/message\") {\n      const message = (event.data as { message?: DshMessage } | undefined)?.message;\n      if (!message) continue;\n      const text = stripInjectedMemory(textOf(message)).trim();\n      if (text) turns.push({ role: \"assistant\", content: text, ...stamp });\n    } else if (event.type === \"tool/call\") {\n      const call = event.data as { name?: string; arguments?: string } | undefined;\n      if (!call?.name) continue;\n      turns.push({\n        role: \"action\",\n        content: actionLine(call.name, parseArgs(call.arguments)),\n        ...stamp,\n      });\n    }\n  }\n  return turns;\n}\n\n/** `tool/call.arguments` is the model's RAW JSON string, unparsed by design. */\nfunction parseArgs(raw: string | undefined): unknown {\n  if (!raw) return undefined;\n  try {\n    return JSON.parse(raw);\n  } catch {\n    return raw; // a malformed argument string still names what the model was reaching for\n  }\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "hindsight-integrations/coding-agents/src/core/transcript-util.ts",
      "content": "/** Shared transcript-rendering helpers used by both the Claude (transcript.ts) and Codex\n *  (transcript-codex.ts) session readers. */\n\n/** Cap on any single rendered tool input or tool result (mirrors v1's 2000-char cap): small\n *  edits/commands are captured verbatim while a giant Write/output is bounded. */\nexport const TOOL_TEXT_CAP = 2000;\n\n/** Injected context — stripped from retained text so a write-back never re-ingests its own\n *  injected memory (a retain→reflect feedback loop). Covers every block the hooks inject, PLUS\n *  the host's own hook-transport wrappers, which arrive as ordinary USER messages and would\n *  otherwise be extracted as things the user said (#3023):\n *    <hook_prompt>        codex surfaces hook stdout/errors this way\n *    <task-notification>  Claude Code reports a background task's outcome — task id, tool-use id,\n *                         status; measured at 39 of these across 400 local transcripts, each one\n *                         the entire message\n *    <system-reminder>    same class; today it only rides inside `tool_result` blocks, which the\n *                         Claude reader already drops, so this is insurance against it moving\n *  Tag-structural, not content-guessing. The block is removed and any surrounding text KEPT — a\n *  message that is nothing but a wrapper then renders empty and is dropped as a no-content turn. */\nconst MEMORY_TAG_RE =\n  /<(hook_prompt|task-notification|system-reminder|hindsight_memory|hindsight_memories|hindsight_bank|relevant_memories|user_feedback|hindsight_knowledge|hindsight_knowledge_refresh)\\b[\\s\\S]*?<\\/\\1>/g;\n\nexport function stripInjectedMemory(s: string): string {\n  return s.replace(MEMORY_TAG_RE, \"\");\n}\n\nexport function truncate(s: string, max = TOOL_TEXT_CAP): string {\n  return s.length > max ? `${s.slice(0, max)}… (truncated)` : s;\n}\n\n/** Keys tried, in order, to find a tool call's primary target for the compact action line. */\nconst TARGET_KEYS = [\n  \"file_path\",\n  \"path\",\n  \"notebook_path\",\n  \"command\",\n  \"pattern\",\n  \"query\",\n  \"url\",\n  \"name\",\n  \"id\",\n] as const;\n\nconst ACTION_TARGET_CAP = 100;\n\n/**\n * Compact one tool call into an action line: the tool name plus its primary target — a file path,\n * command, pattern, … — with NO full arguments and NO output (e.g. `Edit boltons/strutils.py`).\n * Retaining raw args/outputs buries the session's decisions in mechanical noise; the extractor only\n * needs WHAT was touched.\n */\nexport function actionLine(tool: string, input: unknown): string {\n  let target = \"\";\n  if (input && typeof input === \"object\") {\n    const rec = input as Record<string, unknown>;\n    for (const k of TARGET_KEYS) {\n      const v = rec[k];\n      if (typeof v === \"string\" && v.trim()) {\n        target = v.trim().split(\"\\n\")[0];\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n  } else if (typeof input === \"string\") {\n    target = input.trim().split(\"\\n\")[0];\n  }\n  if (target.length > ACTION_TARGET_CAP) target = `${target.slice(0, ACTION_TARGET_CAP)}…`;\n  return target ? `${tool} ${target}` : tool;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "hindsight-integrations/coding-agents/src/daemon-start.ts",
      "content": "#!/usr/bin/env node\n/**\n * Start the local `hindsight-embed` daemon. Spawned DETACHED by core/daemon.ts — never run inline\n * by a hook, because a cold start (uvx download + model load) outlives every hook timeout.\n *\n * Blocking here is the point: this process exists purely to own that wait, and exits once the\n * daemon answers /health. It writes only to the plugin log, so its stdio can be discarded.\n */\nimport { loadConfig } from \"./core/config\";\nimport { daemonEnv, isServerHealthy, preflightDaemon } from \"./core/daemon\";\nimport { diag } from \"./core/diag\";\nimport { log, setLogLevel } from \"./core/log\";\n\nfunction arg(name: string): string | undefined {\n  const i = process.argv.indexOf(`--${name}`);\n  return i >= 0 ? process.argv[i + 1] : undefined;\n}\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const harness = arg(\"harness\") ?? \"coding-agent\";\n  const cfg = loadConfig({ harness });\n  setLogLevel(cfg.logLevel);\n\n  if (cfg.serverMode !== \"daemon\") return;\n  // Several sessions can race to start one daemon; whoever loses simply finds it healthy.\n  if (await isServerHealthy(cfg.apiUrl)) return;\n  if (!preflightDaemon(cfg, harness)) return;\n\n  const { HindsightServer } = await import(\"@vectorize-io/hindsight-all\");\n  const server = new HindsightServer({\n    profile: cfg.daemonProfile,\n    port: cfg.apiPort,\n    env: daemonEnv(cfg),\n    embedVersion: cfg.embedVersion,\n    embedPackagePath: cfg.embedPackagePath,\n    logger: {\n      debug: (m) => log.debug(harness, m),\n      info: (m) => log.info(harness, m),\n      warn: (m) => log.warn(harness, m),\n      error: (m) => log.error(harness, m),\n    },\n  });\n  await server.start();\n  diag(harness, \"daemon_started\", { apiUrl: cfg.apiUrl, profile: cfg.daemonProfile });\n}\n\nmain().catch((error) => {\n  diag(arg(\"harness\") ?? \"coding-agent\", \"daemon_start_failed\", { error: String(error) });\n});\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "hindsight-integrations/coding-agents/src/dsh.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) entrypoint — a native Cordis plugin.\n *\n * dsh is plugin-first: its canonical extension surface is a set of typed lifecycle events, and its\n * Claude Code / Codex hook bridges are just translators onto that same surface. So this integration\n * binds the events directly instead of installing hook binaries — a bridge would cost the same\n * install (neither bridge ships in a default profile) while losing the transcript, the session id\n * and the awaited stop boundary.\n *\n *   agent/session-start  -> RuntimeCore.seedIfCold      (cold-check + background git/codebase seed)\n *   agent/pre-step       -> RuntimeCore.onPrompt        (recall) + the injection as a sourced message\n *   agent/turn-stopping  -> RuntimeCore.onSessionIdle   (write-back of the completed exchange)\n *   ctx.tools            -> the hindsight_* knowledge suite, registered natively\n *\n * ONE dsh PROCESS SERVES MANY WORKSPACES. Unlike opencode/Kilo/Cline — one process, one project —\n * dsh's Web UI creates sessions in whatever directory the user picks, each with its own\n * `session.header.cwd`. Memory is per-repo, so a RuntimeCore (bank, client, seed) is built PER\n * WORKSPACE ROOT and cached, never once per process.\n *\n * The plugin imports NOTHING from dsh at all: every host shape is structurally typed here, and the\n * tool definitions are built in dsh's own registry shape rather than through its `defineTool`\n * builder (see `toDshParameters`). So there is no dsh package for pnpm to resolve inside a profile,\n * and no version to keep in step — any dsh whose event names still match can load this file.\n */\nimport { randomUUID } from \"node:crypto\";\nimport { resolveHostMemory } from \"./core/host-client\";\nimport { diag } from \"./core/diag\";\nimport type { ToolSpec } from \"./core/knowledge-tools\";\nimport { log } from \"./core/log\";\nimport { RuntimeCore } from \"./core/runtime\";\nimport { HINDSIGHT_PLUGIN, readDshEvents, type DshSessionEvent } from \"./core/transcript-dsh\";\n\nconst HARNESS = \"dsh\";\n\n/** Cordis plugin name (loader diagnostics, and the `source.plugin` on everything we inject). */\nexport const name = HINDSIGHT_PLUGIN;\n\n/** The agent registry owns the lifecycle events below; without it there is nothing to bind. */\nexport const inject = [\"agents\"];\n\n// ── host shapes (structural: this package must not depend on dsh's packages) ─────\n\ninterface DshSession {\n  readonly header: { readonly id: string; readonly cwd?: string; readonly origin?: string };\n  /**\n   * Legacy in-memory event log. Present on DeepSeek Harness < alpha.4; removed in alpha.4+.\n   * Prefer {@link snapshotEvents} when available.\n   */\n  readonly events?: readonly DshSessionEvent[];\n  /** Public accessor on DeepSeek Harness alpha.4+ (replaces the removed `events` property). */\n  snapshotEvents?(): readonly DshSessionEvent[];\n  /** How many leading events a FORK copied from its parent (`session/fork`); 0 or absent otherwise.\n   *  Persisted with the session, so it survives a restart. */\n  readonly inheritedEventCount?: number;\n}\n\ninterface DshAgent {\n  readonly session: DshSession;\n}\n\n/** A `user/message` as dsh's pre-step decision carries it. */\ninterface DshUserMessage {\n  role: \"user\";\n  content: { type: string; text?: string }[];\n  source: { kind: string; form?: string };\n  id?: string;\n}\n\ntype PreStepDecision =\n  | { kind: \"enter\"; messages: DshUserMessage[] }\n  | { kind: \"reject\"; [key: string]: unknown };\n\ninterface PreStepPayload {\n  agent: DshAgent;\n  signal: AbortSignal;\n}\n\n/** The Cordis context surface this plugin uses. */\ninterface DshContext {\n  on(\n    event: \"agent/session-start\",\n    listener: (payload: { agent: DshAgent }) => void\n  ): (() => void) | void;\n  on(\n    event: \"agent/pre-step\",\n    listener: (\n      payload: PreStepPayload,\n      next: () => Promise<PreStepDecision>\n    ) => Promise<PreStepDecision>,\n    options?: { prepend?: boolean }\n  ): (() => void) | void;\n  on(\n    event: \"agent/turn-stopping\",\n    listener: (payload: { agent: DshAgent }) => Promise<void> | void\n  ): (() => void) | void;\n  on(\n    event: \"agent/disposed\",\n    listener: (payload: { agent: DshAgent }) => void\n  ): (() => void) | void;\n  inject(names: string[], callback: (ctx: DshToolContext) => void): void;\n}\n\ninterface DshToolContext {\n  tools: {\n    register(definition: unknown): void;\n    /** Registry introspection; used only to log what the host ended up exposing. */\n    schemas?(): { name: string }[];\n  };\n}\n\n/** `exec` as a dsh tool body receives it (only the caller matters to us). */\ninterface DshToolRunContext {\n  readonly agent?: DshAgent;\n}\n\n// ── per-workspace runtime cache ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nexport interface Workspace {\n  core: RuntimeCore;\n  root: string;\n  /** Started by the first SESSION in this repo, then shared by every later one. */\n  seeded?: Promise<void>;\n  tools?: ToolSpec[];\n}\n\n/** `null` caches \"memory is off for this repo\" so a disabled bank isn't re-derived every turn. */\nconst workspaces = new Map<string, Workspace | null>();\n/**\n * sessionId -> agent, so a core's transcript source (which only receives the id) can read the live\n * log back on stop. `agent/disposed` is what bounds it: an agent holds its whole session log, so\n * dropping the entry when the host disposes the agent is what keeps a long-lived Web server from\n * pinning every session it ever opened.\n */\nconst liveAgents = new Map<string, DshAgent>();\n\n/**\n * Prefer `session.snapshotEvents()` (DeepSeek Harness alpha.4+); fall back to the legacy\n * `session.events` property so older hosts keep working. Missing both yields an empty log —\n * which is exactly the alpha.4 breakage when callers still read `events` alone.\n */\nexport function dshSessionEvents(\n  session: Pick<DshSession, \"snapshotEvents\" | \"events\">\n): readonly DshSessionEvent[] {\n  return session.snapshotEvents?.() ?? session.events ?? [];\n}\n\n/**\n * The events this session produced itself — what its write-back saves. A fork saves only its new\n * turns (#5940): the prefix it inherited is the parent's conversation, which the parent already\n * stores, and the child's first write-back used to send all of it again under its own document,\n * re-extracting history the bank already held. The full log is still what the model sees, so\n * everything else (the injection dedupe below) reads `dshSessionEvents`.\n */\nexport function ownEvents(\n  session: Pick<DshSession, \"snapshotEvents\" | \"events\" | \"inheritedEventCount\">\n): readonly DshSessionEvent[] {\n  return dshSessionEvents(session).slice(session.inheritedEventCount ?? 0);\n}\n\n/** Where a session is working. dsh records it on the session header; a session without one is rare. */\nfunction workspaceRoot(agent: DshAgent): string {\n  return agent.session.header.cwd || process.cwd();\n}\n\n/**\n * The memory runtime for one workspace root, built on first use.\n *\n * Bank derivation and the per-bank opt-out live here rather than in `apply`, because the plugin\n * loads before any session exists and the process may end up serving several unrelated\n * repositories. Building one has NO side effect: the seed is started by `ensureSeeded` when a\n * session actually opens, so merely registering the tools never seeds the launch directory.\n */\nfunction workspaceFor(root: string): Workspace | undefined {\n  const cached = workspaces.get(root);\n  if (cached !== undefined) return cached ?? undefined;\n\n  // One shared builder for every long-lived host (core/host-client.ts): the global switch, the\n  // per-bank opt-out and `optInOnly` all land in `cfg.disabled`.\n  const { cfg, bankId, client } = resolveHostMemory(HARNESS, root);\n  if (cfg.disabled) {\n    workspaces.set(root, null); // inert: same agent, no memory (baseline parity)\n    return undefined;\n  }\n  // The 5th argument is this host's whole reason for existing here: RuntimeCore binds the\n  // knowledge tools (and retain stamps) to the workspace it is given, and dsh's process cwd is the\n  // launch directory, routinely a different repository from the session's.\n  const core = new RuntimeCore(client, bankId, cfg, HARNESS, root);\n  // The write-back path reads the log back off the live agent — dsh keeps the whole session in\n  // memory, so unlike opencode there is nothing to refetch over HTTP.\n  core.setTranscriptSource(async (sessionId) => {\n    const agent = liveAgents.get(sessionId);\n    return agent ? readDshEvents(ownEvents(agent.session)) : [];\n  });\n  const workspace: Workspace = { core, root };\n  workspaces.set(root, workspace);\n  return workspace;\n}\n\n/**\n * Start this repo's cold-check + background seed once.\n *\n * Fire-and-forget by design: `agent/session-start` is an emit that no extension point awaits, and\n * the Web UI must not wait on a network round-trip to open a session.
